(b) *The capability group's entrance works again.* `.cap-mbody` named the board's `dropPreviewIn`, which the drag rebuild deleted (7c24fabc). So the group opened with no entrance for anyone except reduced-motion readers, whose override swapped in `fade-in`. The keyframe is back as `reveal-down`, and the sheet's test now fails any `animation` that names an undeclared `@keyframes`. (c) *Copy controls* with a glyph (the session id, the SSO callback URL, the sign-in link and code) keep both glyphs in one grid cell and trade them on `data-copied` ("Icon swap": the hidden one at scale .25 behind a 2px blur, over .2s; `CopyGlyph`, ui/copy-glyph.tsx). The word "Copied" rises in with the check, and on the console's code blocks, whose control is the word alone, it rises in by itself; the resting word returns at once, and the console control keeps its hover underline (`text-decoration: inherit`). (d) *The controller page's replies enter as the dock's do.* The dock's fresh-message rule moved into `useFreshMessageIds`, which both now use, and `.ctl-msg[data-fresh]` no longer needs `.dock-msgs`. (e) *Turns rolls* with `@number-flow/react`, like Elapsed and Tokens beside it (ruling 366(e)), and carries its figure on `data-turns`. (f) *A sign-in step that completes draws its check* ("Success check", sized to the 13px mark): the mark settles in from .8 over .2s while the stroke draws over .3s after 80ms. The dash, 21, covers the check path's length of about 20.2, and the offset lives only in the keyframe's `from`, so a check whose animation never runs is drawn whole. (g) *A refusal the person just caused shakes once* ("Error state shake": the recipe's own stops, legs of 80/80/60/60 ms, 6px each way, then a 4px overshoot; `.refused`). Sixteen boxes were already keyed on a refusal (a counter, or `dupe.n`) so that a repeat is announced again, and they now carry `.refused` too. The class comes from `useRefusalShake` (ui/use-refusal-shake.ts), which drops it once that refusal's shake has played (at `animationend`). Most boxes also unmount while the field is valid and mount again when it turns invalid, still keyed on the same refusal; a class tied to the mount shook on those keystrokes (review, same day: a refused "ab", then "abc" and a backspace, shook the goal editor's box with no click), and on the operator recommendation's acceptance note when a refresh brought it back. The note is also the one box that stands before any click, so it shakes only when it answers one, and the policy page's rows shake only the row refused last. A server error that was never keyed per refusal (the profile editor's) does not shake. The login page's two forms keyed nothing, so a second wrong password left the same sentence standing, as if the click had been ignored. They are now keyed on the refusal object itself (`refusalKey`, login.tsx). The contrast sweep learns that an overlay copy of an element's own words (a `::before`/`::after` drawing `attr(…)` whose ink is its own background: `color: transparent` with `background-clip: text`) is no text-on-backdrop pair; the words under it are measured on their own element, and real text painted that way is still swept. jsdom has no `AnimationEvent`, so React's `onAnimationEnd` listened for the prefixed `webkitAnimationEnd` there; `test-support/setup-dom.ts` shims the event so tests wire it as browsers do. Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 451" (every animation plays a declared keyframe; the status-line and band rules; the copy glyph's shared cell; the dash measured against the icon set's own check path; the shake's legs read off its stops; both ways, every alert keyed per refusal carries `.refused` and every carrier is keyed on its refusal and records its shake, 18 carriers; a reduced-motion answer for each part), `use-refusal-shake.test.tsx` (a new refusal shakes, the same one mounting again does not, a descendant's animation does not count, a reset starts over), `task-detail-components.test.tsx` (the goal editor's keystroke sequence from the review), `runs-panels.test.tsx` (a new phase or step is a new node and the same one is not; Turns on `data-turns`; the session id's glyph flipping in place), `controller-page.test.tsx` (a reply that lands while the transcript is up wears `data-fresh`, and history does not; the sentence's `data-text` equals its words; a new step is a new node), `use-fresh-messages.test.tsx`, `login.test.tsx` (a second refusal, client or server, is a new alert carrying `.refused`) and `operator-recommendations.test.tsx` (the standing note does not shake; the one answering the click does; a note a refresh brings back does not). Canaries, each run: delete `@keyframes reveal-down`; set the dash to 20; drop `.refused` from the reduced-motion block; drop the key from `#lg-err`; drop the key from `TurnStep` or from the strip's step; drop `data-fresh` from the page's article; mark history fresh in the hook; restore the one-frame icon swap; render `{run.turns}` bare; put `.refused` on the acceptance note unconditionally, or whenever `refused` names its card; let `data-text` drift from the words; tie the shake to the mount (`shake: Boolean(refusal)`); drop the hook's reset; drop `.refused` or `onAnimationEnd` from any carrier, or give one a stable key; move the shake's second stop to 50%; draw real text with the band's paint; remove the `AnimationEvent` shim. *(Narrowed 2026-09-26 by ruling 499: the console's code block is no longer word-only. Its Copy carries the copy mark, which trades for the check as every other copy control's does, and it hovers as a button rather than underlining.)*

*(Amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 459: (a) the line on screen when the strip, page or dock opens stands still, and only a line that replaces it rises (`useFreshLine`, ui/use-fresh-line.ts, sets `data-fresh`; a latch, so a return to the first words still rises). (c) the cell is now `GlyphSwap` (ui/copy-glyph.tsx; `CopyGlyph` is its copy case). It serves every glyph that trades with its control's state, busy loaders among them, moves on the individual `scale` property so it composes with a spinner's own transform, and pauses a resting spinner; `data-copied` keeps its name because this ruling's tests pin it.)*

452. **A prompted dispatch refused because its agent is already running says the words are delivered when that run finishes** (owner, 2026-09-24: "say the words will be delivered when the current run finishes", settling the residual ruling 375's controller-door note left open). Ruling 375 records the person's directive before the start. When the start is then refused because the SAME agent already has a live run (the single-flight 409, on the delivering run or on the same engagement), the directive sits inside that run's window, and ruling 203 delivers it when the run finishes, in whatever state it finishes (ruling 211(b), which also withdraws the promise in writing when the delivery cannot start). Both human dispatch doors said the opposite. The person's note read "No run started for <agent>: … wait for it to finish or interrupt it before starting another", the controller replied `[error]` with the same sentence, and the task page answered a 409, so a person or a controller who waited and retried had the words delivered twice. Decided: **(a)** the single-flight refusal is typed (`AgentBusyError`, carrying the live run's profile), because ruling 203 delivers only to the agent whose run finished; a refusal by ANOTHER profile's delivering run keeps ruling 375(b) unchanged. **(b)** When the live run is the dispatched agent's own, both doors write the person's note from one builder (`directiveDeferredNote`: "<agent> is already running on this task, so no second run started. These words are delivered to it when that run finishes.") and answer as a success: the controller `[done] <agent> is already running on <KEY>, so no second run started. Your directive is on the timeline and is delivered to <agent> when that run finishes; do not send it again.`, the task page a toast saying the same, and `run_agent_on_task`'s description names the outcome. **(c)** A dispatch without a prompt has nothing to deliver and keeps the refusal. The @mention path already made this promise in its own words (ruling 203) and is unchanged. Tests: `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` and `project.task.run-agent.server.test.ts` hold a fake run live, dispatch with a prompt, read the reply or the toast and the note, release the run and count exactly one delivery, carrying the words. Canaries: drop either door's busy arm and its case fails; drop the live run's profile from the delivering refusal and both fail. The same-engagement refusal is typed the same way; no test exercises it.

453. **The Apple design pass** (owner, 2026-09-24: `/apple-design whole UI`). The whole UI was read against Apple's design guidance ("Designing Fluid Interfaces", "The Details of UI Typography", and the HIG on materials and accessibility, as the `apple-design` skill carries them). Most of it already held. Presses answer on pointer-down at the sheet's two press steps, menus grow from their trigger, toasts and dialogs leave the way they came, the OS reduced-motion and reduced-transparency settings are answered, and nothing locks input while it moves. Seven things did not hold, and all seven are fixed. **(a) The board's drop flight is a spring that keeps the pointer's velocity.** It used to be a fixed 180 ms `cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)`, which leaves at about four times its average speed whatever the pointer was doing. A card let go of at rest lurched off, and one let go of mid-throw stopped dead first. The flight is now `springFrames` (`ui/spring.ts`): one spring per axis, sampled at 60 Hz into WAAPI keyframes, starting at the release velocity. `createVelocityTracker` reads that velocity from the last 100 ms of `onDragMove` samples. A pointer still for 50 ms counts as at rest, speed is clamped at 8000 px/s, and samples that share one clock tick measure nothing (0/0 would hand the flight `NaN`). The spring is critically damped (damping ratio 1, response .3 s). The slot sits between two cards, so an overshoot would draw the card over its neighbour. Apple ships picture-in-picture, the canonical fling-to-a-slot, at damping 1 too. The closing hole runs on the same frames from rest, so the landing stops moving on the frame the card reaches it. Reduced motion still flies nothing. **(b) A surface closed mid-entrance leaves from where it is.** Chrome starts no transition on a property a running CSS animation drives. So a dialog, page overlay or the dock closed during its entrance got no exit: it vanished in one frame, then held the close for the fallback timer (measured: opacity .50 → 0 with no transition). `pinLivePose` (`ui/live-pose.ts`) writes the live opacity and transform inline, switches the entrance off and forces a style pass. It releases once `[data-closing]` lands, so the exit transition starts from the pinned pose. The on-screen box was measured identical before and after the pin. `useDialog` also plays a running `::backdrop` fade back from where it is (the scrim takes no inline style). The dock pins in `closeDock` and releases in its closing effect. A double click on the dock's button was enough to hit this. The release removes the inline `animation: none`, so every closing rule must switch the entrance off itself. The dock's reduced-motion closing rule did not, and its `fade-in` replayed on the closing panel: up to full opacity, no exit, gone at the fallback timer (review, same day). It now declares `animation: none`; dialogs already outrank their own reduced-motion fade by weight. **(c) A theme change fades, on one clock.** The 2026-09-06 fix swapped the theme under `transition: none`, which is a hard cut, and an abrupt brightness jump is what the guidance says to avoid. For the length of the flip (`THEME_FLIP_MS`, 250 ms `ease`), `setDocumentTheme` now gives every element and pseudo-element the same colour transitions: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke and box-shadow. It lifts the override 50 ms after, so text and the fill under it move together and nothing smears (measured: 59 transitions, all on the one clock). A flip made mid-flip turns around from the colours on screen under the same override. A view transition was tried and rejected. It swallows every click until it finishes (measured, even with `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }`), and the account menu's theme item stays open so a person can click through its three values. **(d) Increased contrast has an answer.** The app ignored `prefers-contrast: more`. It is now a token swap in both themes: `--border`, `--hairline` and `--ring` take `--border-control` (3:1 on the surface, where `--border` is 1.6:1), `--faint` and `--placeholder` take `--muted`, and the translucent chrome goes solid. Reduced transparency now solidifies `.topbar` too, not only `.home-top`. **(e) The translucent bar's edge is a scroll edge.** `.home-top` and the page overlay's sticky head drew their hairline at rest, with nothing under them to part them from. The hairline now draws only once content scrolls beneath, across the first 1.5rem (a scroll-driven animation). A page too short to scroll has an inactive timeline and no edge. A browser without scroll timelines draws the edge for good, which was the old look. **(f) Presses run on the press curve.** 25 transform transitions (`.btn`, cards, tiles, chips, chevrons) ran on plain `ease`, which leaves at under half its average speed, beside neighbours on `--ease-out`, the curve the sheet names for presses. Every transform transition now uses `--ease-out`. **(g) Tracking follows size.** Every heading carried one `-.01em`, two page titles `-.015em`, and the task title none of its own. Three tokens now come from Inter's own dynamic-metrics curve: `--track-title` -.011em (16px, the h1–h4 default), `--track-section` -.017em (20px) and `--track-page` -.021em (28px). Every rule at the 20px and 28px steps takes its step's token, except three one-glyph marks. Text at 11–14px is unchanged: the curve is within .006em of zero there, and moving it would move wrap points across the app. Deferred or rejected: a drag-to-dismiss gesture on the ≤ 720 px dock sheet (a new interaction, offered to the owner separately; *amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 454: the owner asked for it and it is built*); touch-gating the hover lifts (deferred 2026-08-26, and the reasons stand); `font-optical-sizing` (the bundled Inter is static and has no optical-size axis); haptics (iOS Safari has no Vibration API, and the app is desktop-first). Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 453": (a) every transform transition on `--ease-out`; (b) the three tokens equal the curve at 16, 20 and 28px to three places, the h1 default is `--track-title`, every display-step rule tracks at its step, and the exemptions are load-bearing; (c) both bars rest transparent and declare `animation`, `animation-timeline`, `animation-range` in that order (the shorthand resets the timeline); (d) the contrast tokens, the block's place after the dark block, the ratios it buys, and solid chrome under both settings. `spring.test.ts` covers the spring's start, rest, overshoot control, velocity handoff, per-axis independence, the one-second cap and the tracker's window, pause and clamp. `live-pose.test.ts` covers the pin and its release. `theme-preference.test.ts` checks one colour-only clock, the lift at 250 + 50 ms, and one override across flips. Canaries, each run: `.btn` back on `ease`; `--track-page` back to -.015em; drop `.task-hero h1`'s tracking; drop the resting transparent edge; the timeline above the shorthand; `prefers-contrast: less`; `transition:none` back in `setDocumentTheme`. The board's real drag was not driven in a browser (the verification had no signed-in session). The flight's maths is unit-tested, and the module loads in the dev server.

*(Amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 459: a dialog's exit is now softer and shorter than its entrance, 6px and .98 over .15s against 8px and .97 over .18s, and a primary action plays it too, through `useDialog`'s `commit`. (d)'s increased-contrast block also redeclares `--shadow-ring` on `--border-control`, since the floating surfaces now take their edge from that ring.)*

*(Amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 459's deferred dock half: the dock no longer pins. Its entrance is now a transition from `@starting-style`, which `data-closing` retargets from wherever it has got to, so (b)'s pin in `closeDock` and its release in the closing effect are gone, and so is the `animation: none` the dock's reduced-motion closing rule declared: nothing animates the panel at any width or preference. The closed dock's static closure drops from 22 modules to 21 (`live-pose.ts` left it). Dialogs and the page overlay still enter on keyframes and keep the pin through `useDialog`.)*

454. **A finger pulls the dock's sheet down to dismiss it** (owner, 2026-09-24: "build the sheet gesture", the one item ruling 453 left for them). Under 720 px the controller dock is a bottom sheet (ruling 121(e)), and it now takes the gesture Apple's "Designing Fluid Interfaces" is built around. `useSheetDrag` (`ui/use-sheet-drag.ts`) provides it; the dock is its one caller. **(a) Where it starts.** The handles are a grabber bar drawn above the header (`.dock-grabber`, `aria-hidden`: Close stays the named way out) and the header itself, both marked `data-sheet-handle`. A header button keeps its tap, because a drag never starts on a control. The handles take every one-finger touch (`touch-action: pinch-zoom`, with `none` first for an engine without the value, and no text selection), so a pull moves the sheet instead of scrolling the page behind the non-modal panel, while a pinch that starts there still zooms. **(b) How it follows.** After a 10px slop the sheet tracks the pointer 1:1. The slop is taken out, so the sheet leaves from under the finger instead of jumping to catch up, and pointer capture keeps the drag alive off the handle. Pulled up past its resting place it rubber-bands, using UIScrollView's constant (.55) against the sheet's height. **(c) How it ends.** Apple's momentum projection (`project`, deceleration .998) decides: the sheet dismisses when where the throw would carry it is past halfway, and otherwise comes back. A short flick dismisses, and a long pull on its way back up returns. The settle is Apple's sheet spring (damping .8, response .3 s), driven by `requestAnimationFrame` and starting at the sheet's own speed. Past the top edge that is the finger's speed times the band's slope. A dismiss ends the moment the sheet is out of sight and closes the dock without an exit of its own. **(d) Nothing waits.** Grabbing the sheet while it settles, or while it is still entering, catches it where it is. Caught and let go without a drag, it carries on to where it was going, so a tap during the entrance does not throw it back out. Caught above its resting place, the drag starts from the pull that drew the band there (`unrubberband`, the band's inverse). Taking the drawn offset for the finger's pull banded it twice, and the sheet jumped about 60px toward rest on the first move. The entrance keyframe is switched off once the sheet has been held, so it never replays. **(e) One clock.** The offset lives in one custom property, `--sheet-drag` on `.dock`, set with `data-sheet-drag` while the sheet is off its resting place. The sheet's transform and the perched button's travel (ruling 419(j)'s arithmetic plus the drag) both read it, so the button rides a pulled sheet frame for frame, down to its own resting spot and no further (`min(0px, …)`; a sheet pulled all the way out carried it 17px below home, then it sprang back up). Neither transitions while the script drives. The Close button pressed mid-settle still animates: a closing sheet leaves the rule (`:not([data-closing])`). The hook clears the host in a layout effect when the dock closes, so the button returns on its own transition from where it was. That same layout effect stops the spring and the fades. The effect cleanup that also stops them is passive, and a close from a `transitionend` commits at default priority, so a frame could run before it and write the drag back onto a dock that keeps it for the next open. A frame on a detached sheet now does nothing either. **(f) The sheet's surface runs on below it**, off screen at rest (a first box-shadow layer, offset by the sheet's height less its radius). The spring's give and the rubber band therefore show more sheet, never a gap. Listed after the pop shadow, the extension had that shadow's blur drawn across it as a dark seam, seen live on a 115px pull, which is why it is the first layer. **(g) Only a sheet drags.** The 720px block sets `--sheet-draggable: 1` on the sheet, and the hook reads that flag, never the viewport (R19-12). The floating desktop panel never moves. **(h) Reduced motion.** The drag still follows the finger, because that motion is the person's own, but nothing slides after the release. A dismiss fades the sheet out where it is; a return fades out, repositions and fades in. The perched button never slides home under the preference: after a dismissed pull, or on the Close button's `:has()` return, it used to travel hundreds of pixels on its transform transition. The release asks `matchMedia` for the preference (the fifth preference read R19-12's census counts). **(i) `createVelocityTracker` never divides by zero.** Two samples in one clock tick used to give 0/0, and the sheet would have painted `NaNpx` for its whole settle. An adversarial review (four lenses, each finding put to a skeptic who tried to refute it) confirmed nine distinct defects, and all nine are fixed as described above. One of them was ruling 453's and is fixed there. Three findings were refuted as the ruled design: a release still heading up can dismiss when its projection is past halfway, a drag never starts on a header control, and a comment in R19-12's census was stale before this change (it is corrected anyway). Tests: `use-sheet-drag.test.tsx` (17: the slop and 1:1 tracking; a slow short release returns and lets go of the host; a release past halfway dismisses on the frame it is out of sight, at ~210ms rather than when the spring would settle; a flick dismisses from 60px; the settle leaves at the finger's speed; a long pull heading up returns; the rubber band's diminishing follow; a sheet re-grabbed above rest stays where it was caught; a header button's tap; the body and the floating panel never drag; a settling sheet caught where it is; a mid-entrance catch finishes opening; a sheet caught while it leaves carries on out; reduced motion dismissing and returning without a slide; the host cleared in the close's layout phase; and a spring frame run inside that phase cannot put the drag back); `controller-dock.test.tsx` (a pull down the real dock's header dismisses it and hands focus back, and the grabber is `aria-hidden`); `spring.test.ts` (projection, the rubber band and its inverse, the zero-span tracker); `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 454" (the flag only at sheet width, the extension as the first shadow, the grabber and the handles' touch, one value for the sheet and the button capped at the button's home, the Close exit surviving a drag, and no reduced-motion slide home for the button); R19-12's census at five preference reads; and 419(j)'s arithmetic with the drag term, now inside `min(0px, …)`. Canaries, each run: the closing effect made passive; the layout cancel and the detached-sheet bail both dropped; no `unrubberband` on a catch; the spring handed 0 instead of the release velocity; every catch heading for rest; the reduced-motion return keeping the host; a dismiss that waits for the spring to settle; `touch-action` dropped or back to `none` alone; the perch's `min(0px, …)` dropped; the reduced-motion button transition list dropped. Verified in a browser at 375×812, through a harness mounting the real hook on the real stylesheet: the slop held, a 190px drag moved the sheet and its button 190px, a slow release sprang back (190 → 161 → 79 → 57 px) and cleared, an 80px flick dismissed and left the button at rest, a 300px upward pull rubber-banded to −115px, and at 1024 wide the panel had no flag and did not drag. The real dock was not driven in a browser (no signed-in session in the verification).

*(Amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 459's deferred dock half: (d)'s switch-off is gone. The sheet's entrance is now a transition from `@starting-style`, not a keyframe, so `useSheetDrag` writes nothing on a sheet it catches mid-entrance. The (e) drag rule's `transition: none` cancels the rising sheet's transition at the offset the hook read (`liveTranslateY` reads the computed transform mid-transition) and holds it there, and nothing replays after the release, because `@starting-style` applies only to the panel's first style. The hook's comment now states the contract: a sheet's entrance must be a transition its caller's `[data-sheet-drag]` rule switches off, since a keyframe would outrank the drag's transform.)*

455. **The whole-UI interface review's HIGH findings are fixed in one pass** (owner, 2026-09-24: "/interface-review whole UI", then, of the verdict "Block: 54 HIGH", "Fix all 54 HIGH"). A read-only better-interface review covered every rendered route at 1440, 720 and 320 px, in both themes, with and without reduced motion, as an instance admin and as a contributor. It confirmed 67 findings adversarially: 54 HIGH (48 of them escalation triggers), 12 MEDIUM and 1 LOW. One was refuted: Sign out and Rebuild in the danger ink are ruling 149's danger text. Most fixes are CSS in the sheet's own idiom (dialog footers that wrap at phone width, panel titles that wrap instead of reading "A", scrollers with the board's cut-edge cue, long mono tokens that break, menus and popovers kept inside the viewport, the closed rail drawer `visibility: hidden`, focus rings no component rule erases, `.login-aside` in the reduced-motion list). The ones that change behaviour are decided here. **(a) Toasts:** an error toast stays until it is dismissed and carries a Dismiss button. A success toast lasts 5 s and pauses while the pointer or focus is inside the stack. It used to vanish after 2.6 s, errors included, with no way to keep it, and for most refusals it is the only record. **(b) Selection is never carried by hue alone.** The selected filter chip, the board/list and grid/list segments and the console toggles (`.fchip.on`, `.seg button.on`) carry a 3:1 `--border-control` edge, and ruling 365(g)'s subtle fill stands. A selected `.mini-seg` segment carries an inset `--blue` edge. The open controller conversation and the selected agent profile wear the `--blue-soft`/`--blue` selected pair with `aria-current`, not a focus look-alike. **(c) The card's Move menu is also the keyboard path to a slot.** Beside the stages, the board's Move menu offers Move up and Move down within the lane, through the same reorder the drop sends; dnd-kit's Accessibility plugin stays off, so reordering had been drag-only. The menu flips above its trigger when there is no room below, caps its height when neither side fits, and a scroll inside it no longer closes it. **(d) Escape closes what opened last, once.** A popover closed by Escape consumes the key (`useDismiss`, the DatePicker), so an enclosing dialog no longer cancels on the same press and throws away a half-typed New task form. The controller dock also closes on an Escape pressed on a page control its panel covers (ruling 121(e) otherwise unchanged). **(e) A dialog returns focus to its opener even when a field autofocuses:** `useDialog` captures the opener at first render, before commit-time autofocus has moved focus into the dialog. **(f) "Live updates paused" is a strip under the header** (the archived banner's idiom), not a chip in the header row, where at 320-375 px it pushed search, the bell and the account menu off the screen. **(g) Dark `--placeholder` is `#8a91a3`.** It is also the ladder's tertiary text ink, and `#868d9f` fell to 4.49:1 on a hovered row. The sheet's gate now measures that rung on the 5% hover tint. **(h) Copy.** Error pages say what happened and how to recover instead of "Error 403". The re-scan toast reports unreadable files as an error instead of counting them as changed. The New task title refusal names the 3-character rule. The label field states the 12-label cap before it refuses. A filtered activity feed says nothing matches the filters, not that the project has no activity. The rail's violations count says "violation(s)". An SSO provider that is off wears the neutral pill, not "input required". DatePicker's accessible name carries its label and value. Not done here: the 12 MEDIUM and 1 LOW findings, the 197 lower-ranked groups nobody verified, and five axe results the baseline sweep found outside the HIGH set. Those are the controller transcript and the RBAC scroller not keyboard-scrollable at 320 px, the insights `.linkish` target size, the 404 page's missing title and its 6 px overflow. Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "interface review 2026-09-24: the rules the fixes rest on", `toast.test.tsx`, `use-dialog.test.tsx`, `date-picker.test.tsx`, `use-dismiss.test.tsx`, `stage-menu.test.tsx` (placement, the reorder items, dismissal), `board-page.test.tsx` ("acce-17", writ-2, writ-4), `controller-dock.test.tsx`, `controller-page.test.tsx`, `agents-page.test.tsx`, `label-input.test.tsx`, `root.test.tsx`, `require-user.server.test.ts`, `shell-components.test.tsx`, `home-page.test.tsx`, `activity-page.test.tsx`, `insights-page.test.tsx`, `attachments-panel.test.tsx`, `sso-panel.test.tsx`, `controller-admin-panel.test.tsx` and `org-settings-page.test.tsx`. Canaries, each run: revert the dark placeholder, drop `.login-aside` from the reduced-motion list, or drop the closed rail's `visibility: hidden`, and the sheet's gate fails; drop either of the dock's two Escape guards and its case fails. *(Extended 2026-09-24, owner: "fix the 12 MEDIUM findings too". The review's 12 confirmed MEDIUM findings and its one LOW are fixed as well. A locked policy segment shows the chosen value at full ink. The calendar's "today" is a bold blue numeral with no ring, so it no longer looks like the selected day. Commit subjects wrap, and SHAs are no longer painted in the link colour. Review-queue rows (1100px and below) keep the title on the first line. The login page's product statement stacks under the card below 900 px instead of disappearing. Review-queue rows and Home project links are named by their content, not a label that replaced it. The queue tags "waiting on you" from the same answer the board's loader gives its cards (`waitingOnViewer`, decisions.server.ts, which both loaders now call). Store-browser rows open through a real button, with the row actions beside it. The run-prompt placeholders fit their boxes, and each accessible name starts with the same words. Execution branch names use the secondary identifier ink, not the "ready" teal. "Grant scope" is renamed "Re-check scopes" everywhere a person reads it, since it only ever re-checked; the internal ids are unchanged, and the RBAC label is now "Manage the GitHub credential". Information that lived only in `title` tooltips now also reads to assistive tech through `.vh` text: label folds, PR numbers, collision chips, the insights chart and quota rows, resolved violations and stage locks. Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "interface review 2026-09-24: the MEDIUM fixes", `review-page.test.tsx`, `project.review.test.tsx`, `home-page.test.tsx`, `github-view.test.tsx`, `settings-page.test.tsx`, `insights-page.test.tsx`, `activity-page.test.tsx`, `task-meta.test.tsx`, `board-page.test.tsx`, `org-settings-page.test.tsx`, `execution-profile` and the route and server tests that pin the renamed copy.)*

*(Amended 2026-09-24 by ruling 459: the login aside's rise, and its reduced-motion fade, now run on its children (`.login-aside > *`), staggered 100ms apart beside the card; stacked under the card it does not animate.)*

457. **Performance is measured per journey and ratcheted: every hot path has a deterministic budget that only moves down** (owner, 2026-09-24: "https://claude.dev/blog/how-we-made-claude-ai-faster/ let's do performance update like this post"; the five trade-offs in (b) chosen the same day). The method is the post's. The journeys people spend their time in (a fresh page load, opening a task, watching a live run, the live board, writing and sending a comment, the controller) each get deterministic benchmarks: bytes shipped, SQL statements, file parses, React renders and commits, DOM writes, loaders re-run, streams open. Wall-clock never counts, because this machine and CI are shared and a figure that swings with load cannot ratchet. Nine investigators found 77 hot paths, and each fix was written test-first. (Numbered 457: 453 and 454 went to the Apple-design pass and its dock sheet gesture while this pass was on its branch, and 455 and 456 were claimed by the two interface passes open beside it.)

    **(a) The ratchet.** A `*.perf.test.ts(x)` beside the code measures one figure on a named fixture and calls `expectWithinBudget(id, measured)`. The ceilings live in `test-support/perf-budgets/` (one file per area), the client bundle closures in `perf-budgets/bundle.json`, and `node scripts/measure-routes.mjs --check` checks those after `npm run build` (a CI step). The verdict (`test-support/perf-verdict.ts`) fails in both directions: above the ceiling is a regression, and more than the slack below it (0 for counts, 5 % for bytes) is an improvement nobody recorded, so the win must be kept by lowering the ceiling in the same change. A raised ceiling carries its reason beside it. `app/shared/docs/perf-budgets-sync.test.ts` fails on a budget no test asserts. How-to: `docs/development/performance.md`.

    **(b) The owner's trade-offs.** (1) *The bell's list ships with no page.* Pages carry `bellCounts` (unread, plus F19-25's orphan unread counted on the server). `TopBell`, still the one bell (ruling 14), loads `/resources/notifications` when the pointer or focus reaches it and on open, and reloads it once the page has re-read the counts since it was fetched (at once while open), since counts are not a version. UI-14's cap disclosure moved with the list; a first open without intent shows one loading row. (2) *Console lines ride only a document load*, and only the shown agent's display lines. A `.data` load carries each group's window facts and no lines. The console fills itself with one `/resources/run-log?window=1` request, other agents' consoles load when opened, and the stored envelopes load when the raw view opens. The run-end class and the continuity marker are computed on the server. (3) *Live scrollers reserve the scrollbar gutter* (`scrollbar-gutter: stable` on the lanes, the list view, the task page, the console, the controller transcript and the dock), so nothing moves when content starts or stops overflowing; a lane that does not scroll keeps a ~9 px strip. (4) *The Lexical composer is a lazy chunk* behind a stand-in with the editor's markup. It loads on idle, and at once on focus or press; typed text, focus and the caret at the end carry into the editor, and the stand-in already sends. (5) *Console lines go only to the page showing that task* (`taskOnly` routing). Boards no longer receive `run.log-appended`. This ends the owner pin of 2026-09-06 that kept a board as a recipient, which dated from when a board revalidated on a line.

    **(c) What else a reader would expect otherwise.** *Server.* The store readers keep a content-keyed parse memo: the bytes are still read on every call, the YAML and Zod parse is skipped when they are unchanged, and each caller gets its own clone. A GET Request resolves its session and its workspace read once, however many loaders ask. The workspace layout ships the shell's slice; the board's columns are the board route's own loader, and each card is `toBoardCard`'s projection of the fields the board reads. The task loader reads only the timeline slice it ships. A `project.md` write re-projects the project's tasks only when a field they derive from changes (repo, stages, workflow, resolved required reviewers, members), so a task key allocation costs one project row and one event. Each file re-projection is one transaction, and its events publish after COMMIT. `task_events` rows keep their ids across appends, so a timeline item survives a comment; Activity's tie-break is `occurred_at DESC, position ASC, id ASC`. A comment with no `@` skips mention resolution. The run sink writes a line in one statement and patches `agent_runs` only when a fact moves. New indexes: `idx_audit_events__task_action`, `idx_provenance__path_action`. *Client.* Every route declares when it revalidates in one place, `app/features/live-updates/revalidation-policy.ts`: a loader re-runs only for the search params and live events it reads; the echo of the person's own action is skipped when it arrived before that action's revalidation was sent and the action answered inside the live flush's 300 ms, which waits for loads in flight but not for a slow submission (an operator's later reaction still revalidates); root re-runs on sign-in, sign-out, theme and profile actions, a 403 and a document load. A tab holds one EventSource, which the console shares, and a reconnect replays from `lastEventId`. Run lines revalidate nothing: the Live run strip and the controller page read the tail. The dock loads its own data. The dock panel, the account menu and the markdown and console stack are lazy chunks. Board cards, timeline items and console rows are memoised over `useStableRows` (`app/ui/use-stable-rows.ts`, the one structural-sharing mechanism). `Icon` hands React one cached `{__html}` per glyph. One interval per cadence drives every relative stamp and elapsed counter (`useClock`). `useHydrated` reads React's hydration state, so a mount after hydration renders local time at once. Fonts are never inlined into CSS; Inter 400 and 700 (and 500 in the workspace) are preloaded, with a metric-matched fallback face. The client shell ships as a `vendor` and a `shell` chunk.

    **(d) Measured, `main` → this pass** (the budgets hold the numbers; the bundle figures compare `main` @ `639e1e64`, which this pass merged, built alone): the root closure 279,776 → 173,172 B gzip; Home 325,489 → 195,421; the board 374,418 → 243,175; the task page 427,853 → 311,038; the render-blocking stylesheet 56,797 → 36,856. A big task's `.data` 1,048,869 → 13,073 B. A task revalidation's YAML parses 35 → 0, SQL statements 86 → 49, session lookups 3 → 1. Creating a task: 430 → 14 statements, 279 → 1 commits. Renders per console line at 400 rows: 250 → 4. Loader runs per 20 s of a live run: 30 → 0. Board cards re-rendered when one card changes: 40 → 1. Loader runs per five filter keystrokes: 15 → 0; per own comment 6 → 2; per task open 6 → 1. EventSources per task tab: 2 → 1. Rulings whose mechanism changed while their outcome held carry a dated note: 121, 130, 250, 301, 365, 382 and 448. *(Narrowed 2026-09-24 by ruling 458(n): two owner exceptions raised the root and five route ceilings by the bytes of the error page's request id and the one-icon set, each with its reason in `test-support/perf-budgets/bundle.json`.)*

458. **The questions the simplification run left for the owner, decided** (owner, 2026-09-24: "ask me questions about my decision needed ones", then one answer per question; one ruling, lettered). The codebase-simplifier run on `claude/codebase-simplifier-67f858` held back each item below because the change was a decision, not a behaviour-preserving refactor. **(a)** The reviewer-index parser (`reviewerIndex`, `agent-deployments.server.ts`) reads `r<n>` thread ids only, and its tolerance for a `c` prefix goes. `c` was the consultant prefix until 5c13978d renamed consultants to reviewers (2026-07-05), and nothing has written it since. Copies of both data roots held 108 reviewer runs, every one `r`. The only thread ids there that begin with `c` are controller conversations (`cnv_…`), and the parser never sees them, because it reads `kind = 'reviewer'` rows only. **(b)** A failure toast passes `"error"` explicitly; success is the default kind (`push(text, kind = "success")`, `app/ui/toast.tsx`). The rule said "pass the toast kind explicitly", but all 77 pushes that pass no kind are on success paths. So the rule is reworded where it is stated (§UI porting rules above, `contributing.md` §6) and no call site changes; `toast-honesty.test.ts` still fails a refusal-shaped message pushed without `"error"`. **(c)** The five C01-A6 knobs (`VIBERR_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MS`, `VIBERR_DISK_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`, `VIBERR_DISK_LOW_FREE_MB`, `VIBERR_DISK_CRITICAL_FREE_MB`, `VIBERR_GITHUB_WRITE_PROBE`) are read through `getEnv()`. The env schema owns their coercion and defaults, so a bad value fails boot with "Invalid environment configuration", as every other `VIBERR_*` key does. Pass 32 declared them in the schema as optional strings and let each module keep a raw `process.env` read that "reads the live env so an operator can flip it without the process-lifetime cache pinning the old answer" (`env.server.ts`). Nothing outside a running process can change its environment, so that flip never existed, and a mistyped value quietly ran the default. **(d)** The correlation API is adopted. `bindCorrelation` stamps `userId` once the session resolves and `runId` / `taskKey` where a run starts. `currentRequestId` echoes `X-Request-Id` on every response and puts the id on the error page, so a failure a person reports can be matched to the server's log line. Both (`request-context.server.ts`) were exported, documented and tested with no production caller: a log record carried the request id, method and path but never the user or the run behind them, and a person saw no id to report. **(e)** The slot-model names stay: the `task_projections` columns `specialist_json` / `reviewers_json` and `RunKind`'s `primary | reviewer`. Renaming them is a baseline-schema change, and `agent_runs` rows are app-owned, so no rescan can rebuild them under a new `kind`. Instead the glossary (**Slot-model names**) and `data-model.md` say what each means under ruling 98: the delivering engagement, the supporting engagements, and a run's delivery axis, which is not its role. **(f)** The UI ports go ahead. The eight hand-written confirm dialogs move onto `app/ui`'s `ConfirmDialog`, the two hand-written radiogroups (`resource-modals.tsx`) onto `RadioSeg`, and the local SVG icons (`FolderIco`, `UploadIco`, `FolderUpIco`, `EditIco`, `StarIco`) onto `Icon` / `ICON_PATHS`. The run held them back because each one changes what a person or a screen reader meets (accessible names, `data-screen-label`, RadioSeg's arrow keys), and `StarIco`'s comment said the mock keeps it local. The porting rules already ask for one `Icon`, reused everywhere. **(g)** A value that is exported but used only inside its own module loses the `export` (108 at the run's count); types stay exported (236), since most of them belong to an exported signature. `tsc` proves each removal. **(h)** `project.md` and `task.md` share one set of tolerant-parse helpers, on the task file's wording: a missing or invalid field ends "; using <fallback>." and names the value, where `project.md` said "— using a default." The frontmatter prologue (`project-file.server.ts`, `task-file.server.ts`) and the tolerant helpers (`project-file.schema.ts`, `task-file.schema.ts`) were written twice, and merging them waited on one wording because tests pin it. Approved in the same session, and not part of this ruling: three count-agreement copy bugs and the controller Composer's clear-after-send bug are fixed, and the run's third cycle of behaviour-preserving engineering items goes ahead. *(Extended 2026-09-24, owner, in a follow-up round of five questions; 458 was still unmerged. **(i)** The two maintenance periods are set in seconds: `VIBERR_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default 21600, six hours) and `VIBERR_DISK_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default 300, five minutes), each at most 86400, a day. A value that does not parse, or is over the cap, fails boot. The `_MS` names they replace are refused at boot with a message that names the replacement; no live environment set them, only commented examples in `.env.example`. **(j)** The six runtime-tuning knobs (`VIBERR_CLAUDE_MAX_TURNS`, `VIBERR_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `VIBERR_CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `VIBERR_GIT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `VIBERR_TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS`, `VIBERR_SESSION_HOME_RETENTION_DAYS`) get (c)'s treatment: the env schema owns their coercion and defaults, `0` stays a real retention setting (keep forever), and a value the call sites used to replace with the default fails boot. **(k)** `ConfirmDialog` points `aria-describedby` at its body (`useId`), the WAI-ARIA alertdialog pattern, so every confirm built on it is described by its consequence, as the KB browser's hand-written replace confirm was. **(l)** The delete-project dialog carries `data-screen-label="Delete project dialog"` and stays a type-the-name dialog. **(m)** A `test-support/` helper has no test of its own: the tests that use it cover it (`testing.md` §2).)* *(Noted 2026-09-24, on what shipped where it differs from the text above. **(d)** The request id is echoed as `X-Request-Id` on every response the app's handlers answer (the exceptions are listed in runbook.md §"Finding a request by its id"), but the error page does not show it yet. Showing it costs 139 B gzip on the root closure, which every page loads and which sits at its ruling-457 ceiling, so that half waits on the owner: a ceiling exception, or bytes found elsewhere in the root closure. **(f)** Five hand-written plain confirms moved onto `ConfirmDialog`: the user disable, the credential removal, the KB browser's delete and replace, and the agent profile delete. Four stay hand-written. The repository repair dialog, the New task form and the type-the-name project delete each hold their confirm until something is typed, which `ConfirmDialog` does not do. Home's projection-rebuild confirm stays hand-written under ruling 457: Home loads no other confirm, and the shared one's chunk would add about 0.5 KB gzip to Home's budget. The icon port waits on the same ratchet. `FolderIco`, `UploadIco`, `FolderUpIco`, `EditIco` and `StarIco` are still local SVGs, because moving them into `ICON_PATHS` adds about 225 B gzip to the shell chunk every page loads. Both are the owner's to decide. **(h)** A scalar field, or a list field that is absent, ends "; using <fallback>."; a list field that holds something other than a list keeps the task file's "— using an empty list." **The approved fixes** are four count-agreement copy bugs (the connections panel's "lose", the repair dialog's "carry" and its server twin in `settings-actions.server.ts`, and the log-noise "shows them") and the clear-after-send bug in both controller composers, the page and the dock.)* *(Decided 2026-09-24, owner, on the four items ruling 457's ceilings held back; this narrows ruling 457 by two exceptions. **(n)** The error page shows the request id (the second half of (d)) and the icon port lands (the icon half of (f)): `ICON_PATHS` gains `folder`, `folderopen`, `folderup`, `upload`, `edit`, `star` and `starfilled`, and the five local SVGs are gone. The two cost about 139 B and 225 B gzip, so the root closure and the five route ceilings above it rise by the measured bytes, with this reason beside each in `test-support/perf-budgets/bundle.json`. The use-copy hook is dropped: it would have added 170–183 B to the profile, task and controller pages, and only one of them had room. The modules on the task and controller pages keep their inline plurals and backend labels, and `plural.ts` and `backend-label.ts` list them with the reason. `/profile`, which no longer loads `ConfirmDialog`, has its ceiling lowered to its measured size, so the freed bytes cannot be spent silently.)*

459. **The better-ui pass** (owner, 2026-09-24: `/better-ui whole project`). The whole UI was read against the `better-ui` skill: concentric radius, optical alignment, shadows for elevation and borders for structure, image outlines, interruptible motion, enter and exit, press feedback, the theme switch, icon weight and state swaps, and motion restraint. Sixteen read-only finders (ten by principle, six by surface), a completeness critic and six gap finders reported 170 findings. They collapsed to 82 root causes, and three verifiers checked each one: is it real and visible, does it cross a ruling or a gate, is the fix sound. 49 held. Most of the 32 refused were real but outside the skill; the clear ones shipped separately (#338 the continuity panel's console door, #339 the bell's open state, the run button's width and the move-back arrow, #340 the theme controls, #341 in-flight buttons). The test names carry the review's finding ids (F02–F73). **Owner decisions, same day:** (1) ruling 453(c)'s 250 ms one-clock theme fade stays; the skill's snap (transitions off for one frame) is not adopted, and only the second writer of `<html data-theme>` is fixed, in (f). (2) Rows and sub-cards flush in a 22px `.panel` keep `--radius-box`; the ~3px corner swell is accepted (F56 declined, token roles unchanged). (3) The dock's reversible open/close (F20) and a restored dock replaying its entrance (F24) wait until they can be built on ruling 454's sheet. **(a) Nested corners are concentric** (outer = inner + inset, on the six-step scale): a lane under a drag keeps its 22px corners (`.column.drop-over` set its own 16); the palette's rows take `--radius-card` inside the 22px card; the account menu pads .25rem like the other menus; the lightbox picture and code reader take `--radius-box`; the dock composer sits 6px in from the panel's bottom corners on desktop (the phone sheet keeps its 12px gutter, its corners are square); `.seg` insets its segments 2px like `.cap-seg` and `.mini-seg`, with segment padding traded so the control keeps its height; the date picker pads .375rem; the colour-swatch menu takes `--radius-panel` around its round swatches; schedule rows are a divided list instead of a third nested box; a code block that ends a controller reply or a collapsed comment squares the corner it shares. **(b) Optical alignment.** A control with a leading or trailing glyph pads that side 2px less than the text side (`.btn`, `.btn.sm`, `.seg`, `.fchip`, `.rev-add`, `.meta-edit-btn`, `.tl-attach-chip`, the caret triggers `.own-btn`, `.rsel-btn`, `.stage-menu-btn`, `.project-switch`; a trailing glyph is marked `ico-end`), as `.chip` already did; the board's filter input is left alone (its glyph faces an empty field). Text-only chips are centred again (`.pick-chip` trims only when it leads with a glyph, `.chip.more`). Pills that lead with a dot or glyph trim their leading side. `flag`, `hand` and `sparkle` (the Claude mark) are redrawn on the 24px centre, a departure from the mock. A glyph in a plain-text hint sits on the first line's cap height, not the baseline, and the credential card's ok line puts its check on the first line like its warning twin. **(c) What floats is edged by a translucent ring, and images carry an outline.** `--shadow-ring` is pure black at 6% (white at 8% on dark) instead of the opaque `--ring`. The dialogs, palette, page overlay and dock panel wore two edges, a 1px `--border` and the ring inside `--shadow-pop`; the menus had only their opaque border, which on dark was their one edge. Every floating surface now keeps a transparent 1px border (its box, and the frame forced-colors mode draws, do not move) and takes its edge from the ring; menus add the ring to `--shadow-menu` themselves. Ruling 453(d)'s increased-contrast block redeclares `--shadow-ring` on `--border-control`. `--image-outline` (black 10% light, white 10% dark, 1px, offset -1px) edges markdown images, the lightbox picture and attachment thumbnails, which now sit .25rem inside their tile so the picture keeps all four edges. The toggle knob and `.fm-act` shadows are pure black instead of mixed from `--fg`, which turned into light glows on dark; the dark knob takes the ring. **(d) Presses and hovers.** Every press is owned by the element pressed and interpolates: about thirty controls that scaled with no `transform` leg in their transition, or had no press at all while their siblings did, now press on `--ease-out` at .96 (controls) or .99 (surfaces), never below .95 (`.fm-act` .94, the pin star .9 and the dock trigger .94 are .96; the perched phone trigger is .77 × .96). A container no longer dips for a press on something inside it (the board's list row, a project card or row when the pin is pressed). Controls that cannot act do not hover or press: `aria-disabled` buttons, inert decision options, a disabled ✕ (a refused one at the disabled step .45; the member row being removed, read off the request's intent and user id, marks `aria-busy` and takes the busy step .7 as `.rev-x`, `.stage-menu-btn` and `.deploy-row` do, while the rows merely waiting keep ruling 368's sibling step). Hover changes colour, not position, on everything hovered all day: `.btn` lost its 1px lift, list rows their 2px slide, the pin star its grow, `.fm-act` its lift; the lift stays on tiles chosen once (`.pj-card`, `.org-tile.go`, `.be-opt`). The GitHub sign-in button, whose resting border is already the hover border, moves its fill toward the surface instead. `.seg` gained the hover its sibling segment families had. **(e) Enter and exit.** A dialog travels a fixed 8px in and leaves softer and shorter, 6px and .98 over .15s, instead of 4% of its own height both ways (about 31px on the page overlay). A dialog's primary action plays the exit too: `useDialog` returns `commit(fn)`, which runs the action once, then the animated close (with ruling 453(b)'s live-pose pin), and callers no longer clear their own state inside the action; a second commit while closing is dropped, and a confirm keeps the words it opened with while it fades. The mobile drawer's scrim fades with the drawer instead of snapping, and the top bar and dock come back only after it has faded; the drawer still becomes visible at once on open (ruling 455's acce-13), since a visibility transition of any length starts hidden and the nav takes focus on that frame. The bell badge pulses only when the count rises while the bell is on screen (`data-arrived`), not on every mount or when reading lowers it, and its reduced-motion answer now reaches it. The live status line (ruling 451(a)) stands still on first paint and rises only when a new line replaces it (`useFreshLine`, `data-fresh`). The typed @-mention and agent-picker listboxes appear at once, like the palette. Beside the card (900px and up) the login page staggers its pitch after it: the mark and title, then the paragraph, then the points, 100ms apart; stacked under the card it does not move, and under reduced motion the parts fade. **(f) One writer of `<html data-theme>`.** Layout rendered `data-theme` from live loader data, a second writer that re-applied the confirmed theme on every revalidation and skipped `setDocumentTheme`, so a flip could snap back or skip 453(c)'s fade. React now renders the attribute once and freezes it (the server renders the preference; the browser keeps what `<html>` already carries), and `setDocumentTheme` is its only writer after first paint. **(g) Icons.** A glyph takes its label's weight: stroke 2 beside 500–600 labels and 2.5 beside 700–800, set in CSS beside `svg.ico`; `icon.tsx`'s 1.7 stays for 400 labels, icon-only controls and tiles, and a chip's own glyph is scoped so the agent tile it leads with keeps 1.7. The four disclosures that drew a caret from two CSS borders use the set's chevron, one rule (`.ico.disc-chev`) turned by its own `<details>`. Every busy state spins `loader` (Rebuild spun a memory chip). Google's typed 800-weight "G" is a one-colour `google` glyph on the grid. The wait row's glyph rule no longer restyles the Viberr chip's mark, the Agents page's running dot paints (it had no rule) and pulses on ruling 457's `::after` ring, and the login bullets are the set's arrow. **(h) A glyph that changes with its control cross-fades in place.** `GlyphSwap` (`ui/copy-glyph.tsx`; ruling 451(c)'s `CopyGlyph` is now its copy case) keeps both glyphs in one cell and trades them on the individual `scale` property (.25, 2px blur, .2s, `--ease-out`, 451(c)'s values for a 13–15px glyph), so a spinning loader's own `transform` is untouched and a resting loader is paused. Ten controls moved from a one-frame ternary to it (busy loaders, Run → Schedule, Archive → Restore among them). Grant chips always hold their check's slot, so granting no longer grows the chip and reflows the row; the backend picker's check and the wait row's live-to-ended glyph use the same recipe. It also draws the in-flight loaders that ruling 368's 2026-09-24 extension (#341) put on the buttons that start a request: the loader cross-fades in, spinning, beside the label that names the work. A control that trades two marks with its state and also shows a loader while busy (the run starts, Archive, Attach/Rotate) nests them through `GlyphSwap`'s `busy` cell. `GlyphSwap` is memoised, so drawing both marks costs the task page no renders: 49 against ruling 457's ceiling of 51, which the ratchet lowers to 49. Glyphs that are verdicts read from loader data (a stale-cache clock, a scope check) do not animate. An adversarial review of the diff (six lenses, two verifiers each) confirmed ten fixes, all applied: the busy step on the member ✕, the GitHub hover, the pick-chip and run-selector stroke scoping, the locks beside bold field labels, two comments, one test that could not fail, the confirm's frozen words, and these docs. Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 459" (eight blocks, one per part: concentric math read from the sheet, trims measured against their text side, ring and outline tokens in both themes and in the contrast block, every press guarded and transitioned, no hover movement on the frequent list, dialog travel and exit values, one stroke table checked against each label's weight, the chevron rule, the swap cell), and component tests for `useDialog.commit`, `useFreshLine`, `GlyphSwap`, the frozen theme writer (`root-theme-writer.test.tsx`), the bell's arrivals, the grant chips and the confirms. Every new assertion was canaried: the fix broken, the test seen failing, the file restored. The pass merged main twice while it ran (rulings 455, 457 and 458, #337–#342). Both sides were kept: the shared `ConfirmDialog` that ruling 458 moved six confirms onto plays the exit through `commit`, and the press-ownership check reads `RadioSegOption` as the one button it renders. The pass adds about 1.3 KB of CSS and 1.3–1.9 KB to each closure (gzip), so ruling 457's bundle ceilings are raised by exactly that, with the reason beside each in `test-support/perf-budgets/bundle.json`.

*(Extended 2026-09-24: the deferred dock half, owner decision (3), built on ruling 454's sheet (owner, same day: "do the two dock fixes now"). **F20: the open and the close turn around.** The panel's entrance is a transition started from `@starting-style`. It used to play the `dock-in` and `dock-sheet-in` keyframes, and both are deleted. On desktop it starts from opacity 0 and `translateY(8px) scale(.97)` over .18s; on the sheet it starts at full opacity from `translateY(100%)` over .22s. `[data-closing]` is the far end of the same transition. It sets its own shorter duration and no property list: `translateY(6px) scale(.98)` and opacity 0 over .12s, and `translateY(100%)` over .15s on the sheet. Ruling 121(e)'s .18s in and .12s out are unchanged. A click on the trigger while the panel leaves takes the close back. It drops `data-closing`, the panel retargets to its open pose from wherever it has got to, and the closing effect's cleanup drops its `transitionend` listener and fallback timer. The click counts as the person's own open (`openedByUser`), and it re-asserts `open`: the exit can already have ended, its `transitionend`, fallback timer or a pull's dismiss having queued `setOpen(false)` at default priority, which renders a task after a queued click runs, so the click's own `setOpen(true)`, applied after it, keeps the panel mounted and the composer it focuses in place. Focus goes in through `focusInside`, because `open` is re-asserted, never changed, and the focus effect does not run. One click is one toggle: the branch returns before the close below it. A pointer close also ends the sheet gesture: the dock passes `open && !closing` to `useSheetDrag`, so the hook's closed layout effect stops a return spring, a dismiss spring or a reduced-motion fade and clears `data-sheet-drag` in the close's own commit. Left running, a take-back dropped `[data-closing]` under the drag rule's `transition: none` and snapped the sheet and its perched trigger onto the spring's offset, and a dismiss spring went on to close the dock the person had kept open. With nothing animating the panel, the dock no longer pins its live pose (ruling 453(b), amended). `useSheetDrag` no longer switches an entrance off on a sheet it catches (ruling 454(d), amended). Reduced motion fades the panel over .12s both ways at both widths, starting from `@starting-style` opacity 0. Its closing rule restates the .12s: the 720px closing rule is one attribute heavier than the reduced `.dock .dock-panel` and would otherwise hand the fade the sheet's .15s. **F24: a restored dock appears in place.** The restore effect sets `restoredOpen` when the stored answer opened the panel and no click beat the read, and keeps a `true` an earlier run set: under StrictMode (the dev server) the effect runs twice, and the second run reads the "0" the `[open]` write stored in between. `.dock` carries `data-restored` while the panel is open and restored. Only the trigger clears it, on its own open or when it takes a close back (under the mark the way back would snap). A close never clears it: the attribute is gated on `open`, so it leaves with the panel. `.dock[data-restored] .dock-panel:not([data-closing]) { transition: none }` shows the panel without its entrance. It is heavier than every panel rule, so it wins at both widths and under the preference, and a later pointer close still animates. In the 720px block, `.dock[data-restored] .dock-fab:not(:active) { transition: none }` lands the trigger on its perch instead of flying it there. A press still eases, and the `:has()` return, of equal weight and later in the sheet, still carries the trigger home on the sheet's clock. Tests: `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 459: the dock's deferred half" resolves the real cascade (weight, then source order, then the `transition` shorthand against its longhands) for the panel and the trigger in each state, at both widths and under reduced motion, against a two-way table of every rule on either. `controller-dock.test.tsx` covers a reversal (the panel stays, `data-closing` goes, focus goes in, the close survives `transitionend` and the fallback timer, and the next click closes), a close that writes nothing on the panel, the restored mark, a click that beat the read, the mark kept through a close, the mark dropped by a reversal, a take-back click that lands after the exit's `transitionend` but before its render (one `act` holds both), the mark under StrictMode, and at sheet width a close that interrupts a pull's return spring (the host is let go at the close and stays clear through the take-back) or its dismiss throw (the taken-back dock stays open). `use-sheet-drag.test.tsx` covers a mid-entrance catch that writes nothing on the sheet. The e2e `08-controller-dock.spec.ts` reloads with the dock open and finds no animation running and no transition to run, and clicks the trigger twice two frames apart, inside an exit stretched to 1s on the panel's inline style (two frames on a loaded machine can land further apart than the real .12s), and finds the dock still open. Canaries, each run: 14 on the stylesheet and 15 on the component and the hook. Ruling 457's closed-dock ceiling is lowered from 22 modules to 21. The stylesheet grows by 37 B gzip, and six bundle ceilings are raised by exactly the measured bytes (37–52 B each) with the reason beside each in `test-support/perf-budgets/bundle.json`. At 1280 wide the entrance is two 180ms transitions and the close two 120ms ones. A close 60ms into the entrance leaves from opacity .9, not in one frame. Taken back 40ms into the exit, the panel turns around on the reverse-shortened .18s (168ms) and ends at rest. At sheet width the rise and the trigger's flight are 220ms and the close 150ms. A catch 80ms in cancels the rise and holds the sheet at 28px, and a release at rest replays nothing. A restored panel and trigger run nothing, and their close still runs. A timeline file that is not an image is now `.tl-attach-file`, the image tile's frame with a page glyph in the picture's place, its extension on a label (`.tl-attach-ext`) tinted in the pill tones by its language family (`fileFamily`, over the code reader's `languageForName`, so a name the reader learns is tinted with no second list): as pills, the row stretched them into ellipses beside an image tile.)*

460. **Every agent process runs as its person's own OS user, and the store lives where file permissions bind** (owner, 2026-09-24: "Full fix", for finding F40-1 of pass 40). The server runs as `node` (uid 1000) and spawned every Claude and Codex CLI as `node` too. Measured in `viberr-app-1` on 2026-09-24: `/proc/7/environ` (the server) holds `VIBERR_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `VIBERR_SESSION_SECRET`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `VIBERR_SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, readable by uid 1000 and refused to uid 65534, so a different uid protects the process; `/data/state/projection.sqlite` (sealed PATs and keys, which that key opens) and every `runtimes/users/<id>/claude-home` sign-in were readable; and the store sat on the macOS VirtioFS bind mount `./docker-data`, which enforces no permissions between uids (uid 65534 read a 0600 file owned by 1000; `ls -l` showed every entry as owned by whoever read it). So a separate uid alone could not protect `/data`. AGENTS.md's "secrets never reach agent environments" was true of the env Viberr hands a run and false of what a run could read. Breaking changes were welcome (pre-production). The rule: the credential principal of a run (ruling 127) is also the OS user its processes run as; one small setuid launcher is the only privileged step; and the store moves to a named volume.

    **(a) The uid.** Each person gets a stable agent uid, allocated once and sequentially from 20001 by `agentUidFor` in a table of its own, `agent_os_users (user_id PRIMARY KEY, os_uid UNIQUE, created_at)`, in the baseline and in `BASELINE_TABLES` for older roots. The spec's example was a `users.os_uid` column; it is a table because the `users` row is hard-deleted with the account while that account's transcripts stay on disk owned by its uid, and `MAX + 1` over a column would hand the uid, and those files, to the next person. Rows are never deleted and there is deliberately no foreign key. Every agent shares the primary group `viberr-agents` (gid 20000); `node` is a supplementary member (image `usermod`). The numbers are the Dockerfile's global ARGs (`VIBERR_AGENT_UID_FLOOR`, `_MAX` 59999, `VIBERR_AGENT_GID`, `VIBERR_DATA_ROOT`), compiled into the launcher; `agent-isolation.server.ts` holds the same three and a test pins them to the ARG defaults.

    **(b) The launcher.** `tools/viberr-launch/viberr-launch.c`, compiled with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` in its own `launcher` build stage and installed as `/usr/local/libexec/viberr-launch`, root:node 4750 (agents are not in group `node`, so they cannot run it). The spec said gcc was already in the final stage. It was, in an image built on an older base; the current `node:26-slim` has no compiler, and none of the runtime packages pulls one in (measured: the first build failed with `gcc: not found`). The stage uses the same base, so the binary links against the glibc it runs on. The uid range, gid, the server's ids and the data root are compiled in; nothing is read from the environment but the three `VIBERR_LAUNCH_*` names, which it removes before it execs anything. Verbs: *exec* (when `VIBERR_LAUNCH_EXEC` is set) refuses a uid outside the range or a relative exec path, then forks. The **child** makes the agent's own process group, drops privileges with `setgroups(0)`, `setgid(20000)`, `setuid(uid)` and reads every id back (the saved uid too, and `setuid(0)` must fail), sets `PDEATHSIG` to SIGKILL after the uid change (which would clear it), sets umask 0007, and `execv`s the binary with argv[1..] passed through untouched (argv[0] becomes the exec path, which Codex's own arg0 dispatch needs). The **parent** keeps root as its effective uid, so it may signal the agent, and `node` as its real uid, so the server may signal it. It sets `PDEATHSIG` SIGTERM so a dying server takes its runs down, takes TERM, INT, HUP, QUIT and USR1 synchronously and relays each to the agent's group, escalates a relayed SIGTERM to SIGKILL after 5 s, treats **SIGUSR2 as "SIGKILL the whole group"**, SIGTERMs whatever is left in the group once the agent exits, hands `VIBERR_LAUNCH_HOME` back (e), and exits with the agent's status (128 + signal when signalled). The child leads the group rather than the launcher, a small departure from the spec: a relay can then never reach the relayer, and a Codex launcher, which the SDK spawns non-detached inside the server's own group, can never signal the server. *prepare-home* `<uid> <path>` resolves the path component by component from a real `<root>/runtimes/users` with `openat(O_NOFOLLOW)`. It creates a missing directory with the server's filesystem ids (a root-created one would belong to root) and refuses a path whose directories belong to someone other than the uid or the server. It then walks the entry, never following a symlink: the owner becomes the uid, the group `node`, directories 2770, files gain group read AND write (the spec said read: the server also updates the Codex state database, ruling 199) and lose setuid/setgid. Entries owned by root or by another agent are left alone, so a planted hard link cannot turn it, and so is a server-owned file with more than one link. *reap* `<0|TERM|KILL> <marker>…` replaces the spec's `--reap <pid>`, because the server cannot read an agent's environment and so cannot find the pid. As root it signals every process whose real and effective uid are in the agent range and whose environment carries `VIBERR_RUN_ID=<marker>`, and prints each pid. The container holds no `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`, so root reads another uid's `/proc/<pid>/environ` only by borrowing that uid's filesystem ids (`setfsuid`/`setfsgid`) for the one read, and a pidfd pins each process so a recycled pid is never signalled. *probe* `<path>` drops to the reserved uid 20000 (floor − 1) and tries to open the path: exit 0 when refused, 3 when readable.

    **(c) Both backends, the compaction and the sign-in go through it.** `startRun`, the one funnel, calls `agentLaunchFor` whenever this server launches agents. It allocates the principal's uid and hands their runtime root, the vendor home and their agent `$HOME` (`runtimes/users/<userId>/home`, new: `/home/node` is not an agent's to write, and npm's cache and a `git config --global` go there) to the uid through `--prepare-home`; each is skipped when already theirs, so the common case is three `lstat`s. It then sets `RunSpec.agent` and `HOME` on the run's env. *Claude:* `spawnClaudeCli` spawns the launcher detached, with the SDK's command resolved to an absolute path in `VIBERR_LAUNCH_EXEC`, and maps the server's SIGKILL to SIGUSR2 (`launchedSignal`), because a SIGKILL of the launcher alone would leave the agent's processes under a uid the server cannot signal. *Codex:* `new Codex({ codexPathOverride: <launcher>, env })`, with `VIBERR_LAUNCH_EXEC` = the SDK's own vendored binary from `codexVendor()`, the one resolver the app-server compaction also reads. The SDK prepends its helper directory (`codex-path/`, `rg`) only when it resolves the binary itself, so the adapter prepends it for the override (ruling 174 had rejected an override partly for that reason). The Codex run home the server forks is handed to the uid before the CLI starts, and at the settle before the server reads it, and the written-back `auth.json` is handed back after. The completion compaction's `codex app-server`, and the hosted sign-in with its status check and the vendor logout (`vendorCommand`), all run through the launcher as the person, and so does the model-catalog probe, which runs the vendored CLI against the viewer's own `claude-home` (note (l)). No git runs as `node` in a workspace (note (k)). What the server does itself stays `node`: the git of the repositories it owns (the project mirror, a stage), the stdio MCP probes, reading transcripts.

    **(d) The store layout, enforced by the server at boot** (`bootAgentIsolation` → `enforceStoreLayout`; the server owns the tree, so chmod and chgrp need no privilege). `/data` is 0750 in group `viberr-agents` (the spec said `node:node`, which agents could not traverse to reach anything). `state/`, `audit-exports/` and the raw run logs `runtimes/claude|codex/` are 0700. `runtimes/` is 0750 and `runtimes/users/` 0710 in the agent group. `agents/`, `kb/`, `skills/` and `projects/` are 0755, the server's files readable and never writable to an agent. The directories a run writes are `node:viberr-agents` 2770: each task's `workspace/`, `attachments/` and `.operator-scratch/`, and `runtimes/controller-scratch`, `uv-cache`, `uv-python`. `shareDirWithAgents` sets them where they are created, and boot hands a pre-460 tree over once, recursively, and then leaves it. The spec had the server clone with umask 0007. The server spawns git from a dozen places, so instead its whole umask becomes 0002 at boot when the launcher exists: what it writes inside a setgid agent-group directory is group-writable, and nothing it writes elsewhere is in the agent group (its own files are `node:node`). `safe.directory=*` and `core.sharedRepository=group` go in the root-owned SYSTEM git config, not in `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables. That keeps the spec's rule (never a config file an agent could edit) and binds every git invocation: the server's, an agent's shell, and a tool that clears its environment.

    **(e) Homes.** A person's runtime root and everything under it is `<uid>:node`, 2770: their agents own it, the server reaches it through group `node`, and another person's agents are neither owner nor in `node`. A vendor writes its sign-in 0600, and the server must read it (the Codex fork copies `auth.json`; a backup with `--include-runtimes`). So after every launched process exits, the launcher hands the vendor home back (`VIBERR_LAUNCH_HOME`). Boot hands every existing home over: whole when its root is not yet the person's, else just `claude-home` and `codex-home`.

    **(f) The store moves to a named volume.** `compose.yml` mounts `viberr-data:/data` (named exactly, `name: viberr-data`); `compose.e2e.yml` already used a named volume. `npm run store:to-volume` (`scripts/store-to-volume.ts`) moves `./docker-data` once. It takes the writer lock on the source, so it refuses while the container runs on it, and refuses a volume that already holds a store. It copies with a `node:26-slim` helper, drops its own `writer.lock` from the copy (a lock naming another host would refuse the container's boot), makes the tree uid 1000's, and leaves the source. The host dev server keeps `./docker-data` as its own store and no longer shares the container's. Every doc that sent a reader to `docker-data/` for a live instance now says to use the app, `docker compose exec` or a backup.

    **(g) Health says what is true.** `/resources/health` and `instance_health` gain `agentIsolation: { status, uidFloor, reason }`, appended after `toolchain`. `on`: the launcher is installed and the boot probe was refused. `off`: no launcher (the host dev server, the test harness); runs spawn as the server's user; not a fault. `degraded`: the launcher exists but the probe read the store or failed; it is pushed into `degraded[]`, so readiness answers 503, and the reason names the move.

    **(h) Never a silent fallback.** In the image a launch that cannot be prepared (a home that cannot be handed over, a uid past the range) refuses the run with a `run·unavailable` error naming ruling 460 and the launcher's own words. It never runs as `node`. A launcher that cannot exec its binary exits 127 with `viberr-launch: cannot exec <path>: <reason>` on the stderr tail the adapters already carry into the run's failure.

    **(i) Measured** in a throwaway container of this image (`viberr-app:r460`) on a named volume, 2026-09-24: health reports `status: ok`, `agentIsolation: { status: "on", uidFloor: 20001, reason: null }` as its last key; the server's umask is 0002; the layout is as (d). `scripts/check-agent-isolation.sh`, run inside the container as `node` against the live server, passed 34 of 34 checks. As launched agent uids it found: the server's `/proc/7/environ`, the projection database, `state/` and another person's home (a 0600 file and its listing) refused; its own home, a shared workspace, and a file the server created there all writable; the agent's umask 0007, its only group 20000, no `VIBERR_LAUNCH_*` in its env; SIGTERM relayed; a 0600 file readable by the server once the agent exited; SIGUSR2 killing the group with a grandchild; a SIGKILLed parent taking the agent down; `--reap` finding a `setsid`-detached process by marker and killing it. Eight refusals held: uid 1000, uid 0, the probe uid, a relative exec, a home outside `runtimes/users/`, a `..`, a path inside another agent's home, a malformed marker. An agent was refused the launcher itself. The vendored `codex login status` and `claude --version` ran as uid 20500 through the launcher. The same image on a macOS bind mount booted `degraded` with `degraded: ["agentIsolation"]` and the move named. One test-only finding: a child that detaches in the same instant its agent exits can still be in the agent's group when the launcher TERMs that group, so the check pauses before the agent exits.

    **(j) Residual.** `/tmp` is shared by every agent uid, and an agent's files there (umask 0007) are group-readable to other people's agents. Credentials live in the homes, never in `/tmp`, and glibc drops `TMPDIR` for a setuid program, so a per-person `TMPDIR` would need the launcher to set one. A tool that writes a 0600 file into a workspace makes it unreadable to another uid's git, the delivery's included (it runs as the task owner's uid since note (k); the commit fails loudly).
