(`app/server/tasks/task-relay.server.ts`, `operator-actions.server.ts`, `operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `agent-toolkit.server.ts`, `agent-outcome.server.ts`, `task-actions.server.ts`, `specialist-run.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/server/seed/assets/operator.definition.md`, `viberr-app-expertise.skill.md`, `developer-expertise.skill.md`.)

489. **A reply that moved the work resets the react depth, and a depth-capped packet says where the work stands** (owner, 2026-09-25, pass 40, F40-68; spec `planning/discovery-2026-09-24-pass40-akinozer-site/SPEC-489-progress-resets-depth.md`; narrows ruling 362's rework-cycle sentence and adds to ruling 258). Measured live on WEB-8 at 13:55 UTC, deploy 7: the Site Engineer reported its rework done. The new head 178dc22 merged main in (the WEB-9 conflict) and fixed every reviewer finding, and Viberr's gates passed 6/6 on it one second later. The operator's chain had spent its four hops (`OPERATOR_REACT_DEPTH_CAP`) on the ruling-475 conflict hand-off, the owner's rework decision and the rework, so the completion opened "Work stalled: pick a recovery path … hit its 4-cycle depth cap without reaching a boundary". All three of its options re-dispatched work that had just finished, its body carried nothing of the report, and the one step left, delivering 178dc22 for review, appeared nowhere. The depth reset only on an approve (ruling 362), and the packet was skipped only on an acceptable task (ruling 258); a reply that committed a new revision was neither. Decided: **(a)** *Progress is a boundary.* A finished reply whose hop moved the task's head resets the react depth to 0 before the cap is checked, as an approve does. The signal is the one the server writes, never the agent's prose: `headMovedSince` (`app/server/tasks/react-progress.server.ts`) reads the active work revision after the completion's workspace reconcile. The hop moved the head when a `delivered` revision was minted (the reconcile mints one from the checkout's full head and tree sha when the run left a new tree, `nextWorkRevision`), or when a delivery push stamped a revision's `pushedAt`, at or after the finished run's row was created (`created_at`, else `started_at`). The workspace is not read a second time: the revision is the reconcile's reading of it, bound to the tree. Three kinds of head do not count: one reached only through Viberr's own base refreshes mints nothing (ruling 439), an `external` revision is a head somebody else pushed onto the PR, and a `verified` one is the base branch a reviewer judged, which arrives with an approve that ruling 362 already counts. A reply that leaves the head where it was still counts every hop, so a loop that gets nowhere is still capped. A review loop whose every rework commits a new head is no longer ended by the depth cap. The review-deadlock escalation at the third consecutive objection bounds it instead (rulings 204, 237), because it counts a reviewer's objections across revisions. The reset is logged ("react depth reset — this reply moved the task's head") with the sha and how it moved. **(b)** *The capped packet names the state.* When the cap still opens the stuck-loop packet (the task is not acceptable, ruling 258), `stuckLoopStandings` writes three things after the reason. First, the first paragraph of the reply that hit the cap, quoted and attributed to the agent, with heading marks and the dispatch `cc` line dropped, whitespace collapsed, and a cap of 280 characters with an ellipsis. Second, the task's head and whether it is delivered (`taskHeadState`): delivered when a delivery pushed it, the live PR carries it, or it is an `external` head; otherwise committed and not delivered, naming the head the PR still carries. Third, the last gate result on record, as ruling 482's view line ("Gates on 178dc22: 6/6 exit 0 (run by Viberr)"). The verbatim-repeat packet and the failed-run packets are unchanged. **(c)** *The one step left.* Over a committed head nothing delivered, the packet's recommended option is "Deliver <sha7> for review", of a new packet option kind, `deliver_for_review` (the 19th). The spec asked which existing kind performs the delivery, and none does. `redirect` hands the choice to the operator, whose turn may or may not call its tool, and no packet kind stands for the operator's `deliver_for_review` tool. So the kind is new, with no payload. After the resolution write it runs the task page's own delivery door (`manualDeliverForReview` → `performDelivery`, the core behind the operator's tool) under the resolving person's authority, so the push, the PR, the `github.delivery.manual` row and every refusal's timeline event are the ones a delivery always writes. The `run-agents` tier (or the owner) and ruling 240's hold are read before the write, so a refusal leaves the packet open. A delivery that reached the PR lifts the stall's `blocked` readiness, and a supervised task also gets the delivery's "Move to <review>" card. Then comes exactly one hand-off, as in ruling 136(a)'s collision ceremony: a full-autonomy delivery that moved the head re-queues the operator itself; otherwise `packet-resolved` carries a typed `DeliveryServerOutcome` (`delivered`, `current` or `failed`, with the PR, the sha or the delivery's own sentence), which `serverOutcomeSentence` states in Viberr's words. The redirect and send-back options stay beside it, unrecommended, with the hold after them, and a refused composed set falls back to the stock one (ruling 326). The kind is process-only (not appended to the goal, ruling 189), and the generic arm does not re-queue it. `operatorOpenPacket` refuses it unless the task's head is committed and not delivered, naming which (ruling 244's false premise). The `open_decision_packet` kind description tells the operator that the option performs the same delivery as its own tool, and that when its grant lets it deliver, it delivers instead of asking. **(d)** *A ceiling progress does not reset* (the coordinator's amendment, 2026-09-25). Part (a) removed the only bound on a chain whose every hop commits a new head with no reviewer to object, such as the operator re-dispatching a developer that commits each time: every hop reset the depth, so it could run and bill forever. `OPERATOR_REACT_HOP_CEILING` (3 × `OPERATOR_REACT_DEPTH_CAP` = 12, beside the cap in `task-actions.server.ts`) counts every react hop since a person last acted, and a moved head does not restart it. The count rides the chain the way the depth does: the react hands the operator `reactHops` one higher, the drive keeps it on `ctx.operatorRun` for every agent it dispatches, and the drive's own follow-ups carry it on (the `delivered` follow-up of ruling 357 and the stranded resume), so a drive that delivers and stops, or does nothing and is nudged, does not launder the count. Any trigger a person causes carries none, so a comment, a packet answer, a Run press, or an agent run a person dispatched starts the count over. When two of the chain's own triggers meet in the lease queue, the deeper count survives the newest-wins overwrite, as `transitionDepth` does; a person's trigger overwrites it to zero. A restart loses the count, as it loses the depth. An approve restarts the count too, on ruling 362's own argument (a stage cannot be approved twice), and at the ceiling an acceptable task still gets no packet (ruling 258). Otherwise, at the ceiling no operator turn follows, and the stuck-loop packet opens with the same state lines and recommended delivery as part (b), its reason being the sentence "The chain made progress but ran 12 hops without a person or a boundary." When the depth cap and the ceiling are reached together, the depth cap's reason stands, because that last hop made no progress. A drive that dispatches two agents at once still counts each branch separately. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored byte for byte and checked with `cmp`): `agent-completion.server.test.ts` "ruling 489": a reply at the cap whose hop minted a new revision opens no packet, and one operator turn follows (canary: the reset dropped); a reply at the cap that left the head where it was opens the packet as before, naming a head PR #7 carries, with the stock options (canaries: the `since` comparison dropped from `headMovedSince`; every head read as undelivered; the standings not passed); the capped packet quotes the report's first paragraph, names the undelivered head and the gate line, and recommends "Deliver bbbbbbb for review", and confirming it pushes through the delivery's seams, stamps `pushedAt`, audits `github.delivery.manual` and hands off once with the typed outcome (canaries: the standings not passed; the option dropped; the resolution's delivery arm dropped); (d) a chain that commits a new head on every hop, each hop fed the chain state the previous react handed the operator, reacts eleven times at depth 1 and at hop 12 opens the packet with the sentence and the state lines instead (canaries: the ceiling check dropped; the moved-head reset restarting the hop count too; the react not adding one); at the ceiling an approve still continues the chain from zero (canary: the approve no longer restarting the count), and an acceptable task still gets no packet and no turn (canary: the ceiling left out of 258's check). `operator-run.server.test.ts` "ruling 489(d)": a drive the chain starts carries its count; a person's packet answer queued behind a chain react restarts it; two chain triggers keep the deeper count (canaries: the drive's ctx dropping the count; the deeper count kept whatever overwrites it; the merge dropped); the `delivered` follow-up and the stranded resume carry the count (canaries: either carry dropped). `react-progress.server.test.ts` "ruling 489": the committed arm, the `pushedAt` arm, a head that stood still, and the kinds that are not the chain's progress (canaries: either arm dropped; the `since` comparison dropped; any kind counted); the excerpt's first paragraph and its cap (canaries: the whole reply quoted; the cap dropped); the operator's sentence for each delivery outcome (canary: the delivery arm of `serverOutcomeSentence` dropped). `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 489": the authoring guard refuses a task with no head and a delivered head, and allows an undelivered one (canary: the guard dropped). (`app/server/tasks/react-progress.server.ts`, `task-actions.server.ts`, `task-mutation.server.ts`, `operator-actions.server.ts`, `operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts`, `app/shared/packet-server-outcome.ts`.)

490. **A context compaction leaves no note on the task's thread** (owner, 2026-09-25, on the "Context compacted" note by Runtime continuity: "I don't like this note, it's a noise let's remove it"). Decided: this narrows ruling 369, whose (d) wrote the note on every compaction of a task run, and with it the note sentences of rulings 376 and 403. A compaction's record is the `task.agent.compaction` audit row (unchanged: kind, backend, trigger, sizes, whether an anchor was pinned), the run's console line (`system·compact_boundary`, `run·compacted·completion`) and the facts row's compaction count. `recordRunCompaction` (`run-context-events.server.ts`) writes only the audit row, and the run sink no longer takes a data root, which it carried for the note alone. Notes already written stay in their task files and on their threads: the owner chose to stop new ones rather than hide the old. Tests: the note assertions in `run-sink.server.test.ts`, `run-service.server.test.ts` and `session-export.server.test.ts` are deleted; the audit and console assertions stand.

491. **A refused check-runs read is not a pill, and passing gates and checks are green** (owner, 2026-09-25, on the task page's PR card: "checks not readable is a noise, gates passed being dry and not green is a crime on your design"). Decided: (a) *No "checks not readable".* This narrows ruling 360: the PR card, the accept dialog and the GitHub page's PR list show nothing for a check-runs read GitHub refused, as they do for a PR with no CI. Since ruling 482 the verification a person accepts on is Viberr's own run of the project's gates, and the refused read of GitHub's checks beside it is noise. The fact stays recorded (the task file's `checksUnread`, the `checks:read` violation and the credential card's advisory, the controller's `read_github`); the task view and the board payload no longer carry `prChecksUnread`, which fed only the pill, and `checksUnreadPill` is gone. (b) *"gates passed" and "N checks passing" are green fills* (`done`). This narrows ruling 482's "the settled pass is an outline, like every passing check"; the other gates and checks states keep their fills, and the quiet outline (`PillView.quiet`, design pass 2026-09-08) still carries the other settled facts: merged, synced, approved, connected. Tests: the three ruling-360 pill tests (`task-detail-components`, `accept-confirm`, `github-view`) are deleted with the pill. *(Narrowed 2026-09-26 by ruling 511: on the PR card a pass of the gates or the checks is a status row whose mark is filled green, not a pill.)*

492. **A done signal is something the task can show before acceptance, and every door that writes a goal says so** (owner, 2026-09-25, pass 40, F40-69; spec `planning/discovery-2026-09-24-pass40-akinozer-site/SPEC-490.md`, written as ruling 490 and renumbered because 490 and 491 were taken first; records the owner's F40-64 decision and builds on rulings 131 and 269). Measured live on akinozer-com, deploy 9: a person's acceptance merges the task's PR and moves the task to Done in one act (`acceptCompletion`), and the owner declined a post-merge Verify stage (F40-64: "No, keep splitting tasks"), so a proof only the merged or deployed code can show never happens inside the task. Nothing a goal's author read said either, and goals kept asking for such a proof: the operator's own `create_task` option on WEB-16 ("Done when, after the merge and the Workers Builds deploy, a read-only post-merge read … shows the new field's value"), WEB-13's goal ("After the merge and Akin's secret step, a read-only cloudflare-api read shows …"), and the controller's goal-1 link 9 (WEB-12, a quality pass "on the deployed workers.dev build") and link 11 (WEB-7). Each needed a person to rewrite the goal, or an extra packet, before it could finish. The goal fields said only "deliverable plus the done signal" or "acceptance criteria", and `update_goal`'s said nothing at all. Decided: **(a)** *One rule, one home.* `DONE_SIGNAL_RULE` (`app/server/tasks/done-signal.server.ts`, server-only: no client surface shows it). Acceptance moves the task to Done, and nothing after that happens inside the task; a person's acceptance also merges the task's PR when GitHub can merge it, and a full-autonomy operator's never merges and leaves the merge to a person. So a done signal is something the task can show BEFORE acceptance: its gates, its reviewers' verdicts, a measurement made on the branch or locally. Anything only the merged or deployed code can show (a production deploy, a cron run on the merged code, a live page, a production log) is never this task's done signal; that proof goes in a follow-up read task that waits on this one (`blockedBy` its key), created before this task is accepted. Viberr releases the read when this task reaches Done, which can be before the merge and before the deploy, so the read's goal has it confirm the change is merged and deployed before it reads. A goal link whose outcome needs such a proof is split into the delivery link and a read link whose `blockedBy` names it, as goal-1 links 12 and 13 were. **(b)** *Every door that writes a goal carries it*, on the goal field's description: the controller's `create_task.goal`, `update_task.goal`, `create_goal.links[].goal` and `update_goal.goal` (which `add_link` and `edit_link` write through), and the operator's `set_goal.goal`, `open_decision_packet`'s `goalDraft` (`edit_goal`) and `newTask.goal` (`create_task`) on the Claude toolkit. The Codex plan schema carries it on `goalDraft`, `newTask.goal` and the action's `text`, whose description now names `set_goal`'s drafted goal (it named the other verbs that use `text`, and not that one). A grep for every goal field an agent can send found no other door: no specialist tool writes a goal, and a chain's `description` is the chain's prose, not a task's contract. **(c)** *Doctrine.* The shipped `controller-guide.skill.md` gains "Creating a task", which quotes the rule and says to create the delivery task and the read task in the same turn, the read task `blockedBy` the delivery task's key and its goal confirming the merge and the deploy; its "Chained goals" gains the rule for links, with a worked split whose read link confirms the same. The shipped `operator.definition.md` quotes the rule at the acceptance step: before it puts a task up for acceptance, the operator reads the goal and the delivering agent's report, and when either names such a proof and no task owns the read (`read_board` lists none, no link in `goalChain` plans one), it raises a `create_task` option for the read, `newTask.blockedBy` naming this task and `newTask.goal` confirming the merge and the deploy, the read being the new task's own done signal, and puts the task up for acceptance only once a person has answered it; every goal it writes follows the same rule. That is what the operator did unprompted for WEB-14 and WEB-15. Both assets' outgoing hashes are in `PRIOR_SHIPPED_HASHES`. **(d)** *No enforcement machinery.* Nothing refuses a goal for its words, "after the merge" included: the rule is authoring guidance at every door, tested the way ruling 411's `update_goal` wording is. The non-negotiable rules and the fallback persona are unchanged, because the goal fields carry the rule whatever the persona says. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored byte for byte and checked): `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": the four published goal fields each contain `DONE_SIGNAL_RULE`, read through a real MCP client (canaries: the rule dropped from each door, each failing by the door's name; the rule emptied). `operator-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": the same for `set_goal.goal`, `goalDraft` and `newTask.goal` on the Claude toolkit and for `text`, `goalDraft` and `newTask.goal` in the Codex plan schema (canaries: each of the six dropped). `default-assets.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": the guide's "Creating a task" section quotes the rule and its "Chained goals" section splits a link, the doctrine quotes the rule and the `create_task` sentence, and both outgoing hashes are recorded (canaries: the guide's rule; its Chained goals bullet; the doctrine's rule; its `create_task` sentence; each hash removed). (`app/server/tasks/done-signal.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/server/seed/assets/controller-guide.skill.md`, `operator.definition.md`, `app/server/seed/default-assets.server.ts`.) **(e)** *Review corrections* (2026-09-26, before the merge). Two reviewers found the first wording false on two paths, and the text in (a) and (c) above is the corrected one. *The merge.* The rule opened "Acceptance merges the task's PR and moves the task to Done in the same write". A full-autonomy operator's acceptance (`operatorAcceptCompletion`) never merges: it leaves the PR "accepted, merge pending" for a person. A person's acceptance merges only when GitHub can, and a task-key `blockedBy` entry is done when its task reaches Done, merged or not (`taskState`, `app/server/projections/dependencies.server.ts`), and ruling 131(e)'s sweep releases the read then. So the read the rule prescribed could read production before the change was there. The fix is the wording: the read's goal confirms the merge and the deploy before it reads, which a deploy that trails even a real merge needs anyway. A dependency still resolves at Done; ruling 131 is unchanged. *The timing.* The rule said the read is raised "before or at" the acceptance, and the doctrine said to raise its `create_task` option "first" and ended "Never hold this task back for that proof". But an acceptance withdraws the open decision it does not answer (F32-11), the operator's own answers none (ruling 471(b)), and one packet's options cannot both accept and create. An operator that opened the option and accepted in the same turn buried the read; ruling 430's pause covers only the Codex plan. A supervised operator's acceptance card stood beside the option, for a person to apply first. The read is now created before the acceptance, the doctrine stops until a person answers, and `operatorAcceptCompletion` refuses (`noop`, `followUpOptionRefusal`) while the open decision, not yet decided (`awaiting`), offers a `create_task` whose `newTask.blockedBy` names this task. It checks before both branches, so there is no full-autonomy write and no card, the fold into the acceptance stage included; `accept_completion`'s description says so. (d) stands, since nothing refuses a goal for its words; this refusal is on the operator's own acceptance only. Every other open decision is withdrawn as before, and a person's acceptance is not refused (its dialog names the decision it withdraws). No new prior hash: the replaced asset versions never shipped, and a store seeded from them records its own copy in the manifest. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored byte for byte and checked with `cmp`): `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": full autonomy refuses with the decision left open, nothing withdrawn and no acceptance row; supervised files no card; a `create_task` whose new task does not wait on this one is withdrawn as before; a decision answered another way (awaiting its goal edit) holds nothing; once a person answers, the read task exists `blockedBy` this one, the operator's acceptance proceeds with the PR left `accepted`, and the acceptance's own sweep releases the read (canaries: the check dropped, three red; a refusal on every `create_task`; the `awaiting` check dropped). `operator-toolkit.server.test.ts`: `accept_completion`'s sentence (canary: dropped). `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": the rule's new clauses, and neither "in the same write" nor "at this task's acceptance" (canaries: the old opening sentence; "raised before or at"). `default-assets.server.test.ts` "ruling 492": the guide's two merge checks, the doctrine's wait for the answer, and no "Never hold this task back" (canaries: each merge check; the wait; the old sentence). (`app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/done-signal.server.ts`, both assets.) *(Narrowed 2026-09-26 by ruling 503: the goal link split became two tasks, in the same epic when there is one, and the rule's last sentence says so; the doors that carry it are the controller's `create_task` and `update_task` and the operator's three, since `create_goal` and `update_goal` are retired.)*

493. **A gate run's timeline note is its ending, its revision and the gate table, and the PR card and the accept dialog show the same table** (owner, 2026-09-26, on the "Project gates passed" note: "this looks dated asf, no real design … maybe with tables as well? But UX should be excellent"). Measured on the akinozer-com task the note ruling 482(d) writes said the run three times and listed each log twice: under the actor "Project gates" and a neutral "Note" pill came the title "Project gates passed", the bold line "Gates on 84779c7: 6/6 exit 0 (run by Viberr).", "Each gate's log is attached.", a monospaced block of six rows like `install: exit 0 in 2 s · gate-84779c7-01-install-20260925T081253Z.log`, and the same six logs again as attachment files. Decided: **(a)** *The note is drawn from what it records.* `gateNoteView` (`app/shared/project-gates.ts`) reads a note written by the gates' system actor back into its ending (its title, one of `GATE_NOTE_TITLE`), its revision (the sha its line names) and one row per gate (its evidence rows, printed by `gateEvidenceLabel`, which the writer now calls), and links a row's log only when the note claims that file. `mapTaskEventRow` hands the timeline that view as `gates`, with `evidence` null and `attachments` holding only a file no row links, so the page carries each log once. Any other title, or a row in another shape, reads as null and the note renders as before. The note's words do not change, because agents and task.md read them, and notes already written read back the same way: the format has not changed since ruling 482. **(b)** *The header says how the run ended.* The rail node takes the ending (a green check, a red cross, or a red alert for a run that could not execute), the pill reads "passed", "failed" or "could not run" in `gatesPill`'s kinds (a pass is a green fill, ruling 491), and the revision stands beside it ("on 84779c7"). The title and the note's sentence are not repeated. A run that could not execute keeps its reason (`detail`: the note's text less its bold line). **(c)** *One gate table* (`GateResults`, `app/features/task-detail/gate-results.tsx`) serves the timeline note, the PR card's Gates row and the accept dialog's failing gates, replacing the card's and the dialog's lists. Each row has a pass or fail mark, the gate's name (a failure adds its outcome in words: "exit 1", "timed out"), its time and a Log button that opens the log in the in-app reader (ruling 105). A failing row is tinted. On the timeline the table stops at 36rem; at phone width it takes the data size and the Log button keeps only its glyph (its name stays "<gate> log"). The line the PR card and the dialog print above it is unchanged. A project that declares more than eight gates still records eight evidence rows (`EVIDENCE_MAX_ROWS`), so the table shows those eight and the later logs stay files under it. Tests: `project-gates.test.ts` (a finished note reads back row for row; a log the note does not claim is not linked; a could-not-run note keeps its reason; any other note is null), `task-event.server.test.ts` (the view replaces the evidence and the linked logs; a file no row links stays; another writer's note is untouched), `project-gates.server.test.ts` (a real run's projected note reads back as that run), `task-detail-components.test.tsx` (the note's node, pill, revision, table and log link; a pass is green; a could-not-run note keeps its reason; the PR card's table). Each was canaried. *(Narrowed 2026-09-26 by ruling 511: on the PR card a passing run's table folds behind "Show all" under the gates' row; any other run's stands open.)*

494. **A push that moves a task's branch re-compares it, and the compare names the head it read** (owner, 2026-09-26, pass 40, F40-70; spec `planning/discovery-2026-09-24-pass40-akinozer-site/SPEC-494.md`; extends F37-11 and ruling 132). Measured live on WEB-16 (deploy 9, 2026-09-25): at 21:25:48.326Z `update_branch_from_base` found `web-16` level with `main` in the workspace and GitHub's copy (`aafee66`) behind the workspace; at 21:25:48.527Z a poll compared that unpushed copy and recorded `behindBy: 6`; at 21:25:55Z the delivery pushed `20534f6`, whose parents are the branch and `main`'s tip, and nothing compared again until the 21:30:48Z poll. For those five minutes `get_task.baseBehindBy` said 6: the operator commented that `main` was 6 commits ahead and postponed a refresh it did not need, and two packets the owner decided on said "web-16, 6 commits behind main" while the accept dialog, reading GitHub live, said the branch carried `main`. The count was the newest `github.reconcile` row, the row named no head, and only the five-minute poller compared. Decided: **(a)** *A push re-compares.* `recompareAfterPush` (`github-reconciler.server.ts`) takes the task's reconcile lock (F19-19), records a `github.push` provenance row naming the head the push published (`{repo, branch, headSha, via}`), then runs an ordinary pass, whose row names the head it compared. The push row is written inside the lock, so a pass that read the branch before the push and is still running writes its row first and cannot record its older count after the push. Callers: `performDelivery`, for every push that moved the branch (`pushed`, never `up_to_date`), by the operator or a person (the pass audited as whoever delivered, `OPERATOR_AUDIT_ACTOR` for the operator) and through the reuse-an-open-PR path too, once the PR door has answered whatever it answered, on the thrown path as well, before `recordPushedHead` (so a pull request GitHub has not caught up on cannot leave its older head on the file, F39-64) and before the `delivered` re-queue; and `recordBranchRefresh`, which the operator's `update_branch_from_base`, the acceptance ceremony's base refresh and ruling 449's refresh-and-review share, in place of its plain pass. The grep found no other write that moves a task branch to a head: `ensureTaskBranch` creates a missing branch at the base's tip, level with the base, before any work is on it, and its first pass records the count; `deleteTaskRemoteBranch` removes the branch where the task closes (the merge's cleanup, an archive, a no-change acceptance), where no operator turn reads the count, and in the collision ceremony, whose re-delivery is a push and re-compares; the merge and the repository bootstrap move the base. A re-compare that fails (GitHub unreachable, the credential refused) leaves the push standing and writes no count in its place, and the caller says so where it answers with the push: the reply of a `deliver_for_review` that delivered, and the branch update's line, add "`web-16` could not be compared with `main` again after the push (network_unavailable), so the count of commits it is behind stays the one from before the push until the next GitHub pass." A re-compare that ran adds to that delivery reply "Re-compared after the push: `web-16` at `20534f6` is level with `main`.", or, when GitHub answered with another head than the one pushed, "Re-compared after the push: GitHub's `web-16` stands at `aafee66`, not the `20534f6` just pushed, and is 6 commits behind `main`." (`pushRecompareSentence`). A delivery whose push landed but that ended otherwise (the PR door answered `closed_by_human`, `branch_collision`, `nothing_to_review` or another refusal, or something threw after the push) re-compares the same way, and its reply leaves the count to `get_task`. **(b)** *The compare names what it compared.* The reconcile row gains `headSha`, the branch head the compare read, and `baseSha`, the base tip (`base_commit`). GitHub's answer does not name the head outright, so `comparedHeadSha` (`branch-sync.server.ts`) reads it from what the answer carries: `identical` the base tip, `behind` the merge base, `ahead` or `diverged` the one listed commit no other listed commit names as a parent, which holds only on a complete list; a paged list, a dropped entry or an answer with no status is null. A pass that compared another head than the newest row names writes a row even on a quiet poll, as a verdict change does (F37-9), so a row written before this ruling, which names no head, is replaced by the first pass whose compare names a head (a compare that names none writes no row on a quiet poll, and a poll visits at most 20 tasks of a project, `RECONCILE_POLL_TASK_BUDGET`, resuming where it stopped on the next). `get_task` gains `baseComparedHead` `{sha, observedAt, current, pushedSince}` and `baseBehindBySentence`, from `createBaseCompareLookup` (`provenance-query.server.ts`): `current` is false when the count was not read on the head Viberr's newest push published, `pushedSince` naming that push: a `github.push` row newer than the count that published another head (or one git could not name), or a push whose first compare after it, its own re-compare (written in the same hold of the lock), read another head than the push published because GitHub answered before it showed the push, until a later pass compares again; a compare after that first one is GitHub's word on the branch, a head a person moved on GitHub included. It is null when the row names no head, which never reads as current either; the sentence names both heads ("`baseBehindBy` (6) was counted on `aafee66`, and Viberr pushed `20534f6` to `web-16` after that compare, so the count describes the older head. Do not quote it, in a comment or a decision packet, as how far `web-16` is behind `main` now…", or for a re-compare that read the older head "`baseBehindBy` (6) was counted on `aafee66`, not on `20534f6`, which Viberr pushed to `web-16` before that compare, so the count does not describe the pushed head…"). The Codex operator reads the same snapshot. The spec offered `pr.headSha`, the last pushed revision or `workRevision` as the known head, the one delivery keeps current; none is current after every push (`pr.headSha` keeps the older head until GitHub shows a push on the pull request, F39-64, a task with no live pull request has none and a closed one stops tracking the branch; `workRevision` stays behind a base refresh, ruling 439), so the known head is the one each push recorded, beside the compares in the same table and ordered by its ids. **(c)** *The operator's words follow the fact.* The descriptions of `update_branch_from_base` and `get_task` and the shipped `operator.definition.md` (its outgoing hashes in `PRIOR_SHIPPED_HASHES`, the text this ruling first shipped included; the sentence after the packet rule names `update_branch_from_base`, where an "it" read as the packet or the count) say that `baseComparedHead` names the head the count was read on, to check it against the head just pushed, never to state an older head's count as the branch's, and that a decision packet never states a behind count for a head other than the one the packet puts up. Every turn on both backends carries `baseBehindBySentence` and that packet rule while the count is not current (`baseCompareInstruction`), and nothing when it is. The task page and the accept dialog are unchanged: they read the same row, which a push now refreshes. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored byte for byte and checked with `cmp`): `push-recompare.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": push then read, a delivery through the reuse-an-open-PR path after a poll counted the old head 6 behind leaves a push row and a count of 0 for the pushed head, `get_task` reads 0 as current, the reply says so and the pass is audited as the operator (canaries: the post-push re-compare dropped; the operator's task actor passed through); re-compare fails, the push stands, nothing counts the pushed head, and `get_task` still reads 6 but as the older head's, with the sentence, while the reply says the count is from before the push (canaries: no push row; the reply's failure arm dropped); a delivery that throws after its push still re-compares (canary: the catch's re-compare dropped); a pass mid-compare when the push lands writes its row before the push row (canary: the push row written outside the task's lock); a re-compare GitHub answers with the replaced head, the reply names both heads and `get_task` reads the count as not the pushed head's until the next pass reads it (canary: only a push recorded after the compare read); compared head, a count for head A with a later push of B names A, reads `current: false` and says it is not B's, a compare after the push reads current, the compare right after a push of B that read A reads `current: false` with its own sentence while a later compare, a head a person moved on GitHub included, reads current, and a row without a head reads as unknown (canaries: the push row ignored; only a push recorded after the compare read; a missing head read as current; the sentence dropped). `update-branch-operator.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": branch update then push, WEB-16's sequence (canary: the delivery's re-compare dropped); an update that pushes records the push and counts the merge commit (canary: `recordBranchRefresh` back on a plain `reconcileTask`); an update whose re-compare fails says so on its line and `get_task` reads the older head (canaries: the same; the line's clause dropped). `github-reconciler.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": the row records the head and the base tip (canaries: either dropped); a quiet poll writes a row when the head moved and replaces a headless row (canary: the head condition dropped). `branch-sync.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": identical, behind, and ahead or diverged with the head listed before its parent, and the lists that cannot name a head (canaries: `behind` read as the base tip; the last listed commit taken; the completeness check dropped; a missing status read as identical). `provenance-query.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": a push recorded after the count, and one whose first compare read another head, are pushes the count does not describe, a later compare is taken at its word, and a head missing on either side leaves that first compare nothing to check (canaries: only a push recorded after the compare read, the `id > ?` bound this lookup first had; every compare checked against the newest push). `operator-run.server.test.ts`, `operator-toolkit.server.test.ts` and `default-assets.server.test.ts` "ruling 494": the turn instruction on both backends, the two descriptions, the doctrine's sentences, the tool named after the packet rule and both outgoing hashes (canaries: each dropped; "Never call it" restored; either hash removed). (`app/server/github/github-reconciler.server.ts`, `branch-sync.server.ts`, `update-branch-operator.server.ts`, `app/server/provenance/provenance-query.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `operator-actions.server.ts`, `operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/server/seed/assets/operator.definition.md`.)

495. **What the server wrote in a tree an agent can write is the agents' group's to remove, and the emptied root goes with the server's `rmdir`** (owner, 2026-09-26, pass 40, F40-71; spec `planning/discovery-2026-09-24-pass40-akinozer-site/SPEC-495.md`; completes ruling 485, dated note there). Measured live at the deploy-10 boot (`42dc0985`, 2026-09-25 23:12Z): `reclaimTerminalTaskWorkspaces` logged "could not reclaim a finished task's workspace" for the same 15 terminal tasks as on every boot, and 52 `.viberr-plugins/run_*` directories stood in the store's task workspaces, one per settled run. Ruling 485 removes such a tree as its person and then as each agent uid found in what is left, never as the server's user, and two things in those trees are the server's own, which no pass could remove. The skill mount `cpSync`s each granted skill into `<workspace>/.viberr-plugins/<runId>/skills/<name>/`, and `cpSync` keeps the source's modes: the copy's folders came out `node:viberr-agents` at the store folder's 0755 and its files `node:node` (measured in the image: a 0700 folder and a 0600 file come through as 0700 and 0600 too), so the person could not unlink them (`EACCES on …/skills/sourced-content/SKILL.md`, at every run's settle and in every reclaim). And a task's `workspace/` is the server's (2770) in a task directory only the server writes (`node:node` 755), so no agent uid may unlink it, even empty, as WEB-1's is (`EACCES on …/WEB-1/workspace`). Decided, and this is what it changes about "never as the server's user": the server still never runs `rm` on a tree an agent can write; it may open its own entries there with `chmod` and remove an emptied root it owns with `rmdir`. **(a)** *What the server writes into an agent's tree, the agents' group can remove.* Every entry of a run's plugin is made anew with the mode the person's removal needs and is never changed once it exists (`copySkillFolder` and `writeNewPluginFile`, `skill-mount.server.ts`), whatever modes the store folder carries (the e2e store's are `node:node` 755 and 644). A folder is made by `mkdir`, never one already there, under the server's umask (0002 whenever it launches agents; boot sets it) in the workspace's setgid chain, so it is 2775 in the workspace's group. A file is made by an exclusive create (`O_EXCL`, `O_NOFOLLOW`) and its mode set on its own new descriptor, whatever the umask: 0644, or 0755 when the store's is executable. The store's own SKILL.md is not copied; the mount writes it normalized, the same way. The person's removal at the settle unlinks all of it. Rejected on review (2026-09-26): setting the modes after `cpSync` with a chmod walk, which this ruling first shipped. The plugin's folders are the group's to write, and a descriptor opened without following a link guards only a path's last name, so an agent that swapped a folder above for a link mid-copy led the walk to widen whatever of the skill's names the linked folder held. Now a swapped folder can only lead the copy to make new entries elsewhere or to stop at one already there, and nothing it finds is changed. The grep for other server writes under a workspace or `.viberr-plugins` found the rest already removable by the group (a run's and a supporting checkout's folders, made after the workspace is shared, under the server's umask 0002 and its setgid; a checkout handed over from its stage; the gates' folders and logs; attachments; a Codex run home, handed to its person), except `resumeWorkdir` (`agent-reply.server.ts`), which made a missing `workspace/` as the server's alone; it now hands it to the agents' group first (`shareDirWithAgentsOrWarn`), as a run does. **(b)** *Residue the server already wrote is opened, not removed, by the server.* When the agent passes leave entries, `removalPlan` (`agent-trees.server.ts`) runs one step as the server's own user, `chmod -R -P g+rwX -- <tree>`, and the person's pass and the owner rounds run again. `-P` because GNU chmod's `-R` defaults to `-H`, which traverses a link named on the command line (measured in the image, coreutils 9.7: `chmod -R g+rwX -- <link>` changed the linked tree, `chmod -R -P g+rwX -- <link>` changed nothing). **(c)** *The emptied root goes with the server's `rmdir`.* When the passes leave the target an empty directory the server's uid owns, the server runs `rmdir -- <tree>`, which walks nothing. A target still holding entries stays a fault naming the path and the OS error, and an empty one an agent uid owns is left to the agent passes; rmdir's refusal is read like rm's. The seed's reset, which removes each task's `workspace/`, `attachments/` and `.operator-scratch/` as its owner, now takes their roots too. **(d)** *Nothing else changes*: with isolation off the plan is the one user's as before, with isolation on and no person named it refuses, and the error type and its message are unchanged. The module restates 485's safety argument: no recursive remove runs with the server's authority; chmod follows no link, during the traversal or at the tree; chmod refuses what the server does not own, and `g+rwX` opens an entry only to the group it already has (`state/` and the raw run logs are in the server's own group); `chmod -R` has no way to leave out a file with a second link, and the server makes such links itself: its clone of a checkout from the project mirror (`git clone --local`) hardlinks the checkout's objects to the mirror's, and an agent can put one where its person's pass cannot remove it, so the step reaches it. The hand-over before R-seams-1 had put some of those files in the agents' group, where opening one would open the mirror's copy to every agent, so boot's `revokeMirrorWrites` (`agent-isolation.server.ts`) now also puts every mirror file back in the server's own group, which no agent uid is in (agents read the mirror through its other-read bits), and the next boot takes back off any group write the step added. An agent cannot link any other server file it cannot already read and write, because `fs.protected_hardlinks` is 1. That is the host kernel's setting, not the image's (a container reads the kernel's `/proc/sys/fs`): measured 1 in the e2e stack's container on this host on 2026-09-26 (`protected_symlinks` 1 too), and the in-image check fails on a host that has it off. And neither server step runs while a directory above the tree is a link an agent could have put there, through which the steps would reach another directory of the tree's name: one an agent uid owns, or any link in a folder an agent can write, since an agent can move a link the server made (a symlink a repository commits, checked out by the server's clone) into any folder it writes. The server puts no link on these paths itself. This ruling first flagged only links an agent uid owns, which such a moved link passed with no race (review, 2026-09-26). The check is a read before each step, so a link swapped in between is not covered; with no check at all, the in-image check below measured the server opening and then removing a server-owned folder through an agent's link. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored afterwards and checked byte for byte): `agent-trees.server.test.ts` "ruling 495": the plan, against a stand-in view of the tree, takes neither server step for a tree the person's pass removes, opens residue with `chmod -R -P g+rwX` and then removes it as the person, removes an emptied root the server owns with `rmdir` and opens nothing first, does both for WEB-2's workspace, gives no `rmdir` to a target still holding entries (a fault naming the path and the errno) or to an emptied root an agent uid owns, runs the owner rounds before the chmod and again after it, and runs no server step with isolation off or through an agent's link (canaries: the chmod dropped; `-P` dropped; the rmdir dropped; the rmdir for any target; the link check dropped; a server step with isolation off); the drivers, with the real binaries and a stand-in person held to the group's rights, remove WEB-2's plugin residue and an emptied root and leave a tree no one may empty as a fault (canaries: the chmod dropped; the rmdir dropped; the rmdir for any target), open and remove nothing through a link the server made that an agent moved into a folder it writes, and still act through a link in a folder only the server writes, such as macOS's `/var` (canaries: only links an agent uid owns flagged; every link flagged); rmdir's GNU and BSD refusals are read (canary: their patterns dropped). `agent-isolation.server.test.ts` "ruling 495": a mirror file an earlier hand-over gave the agents' group (a second group of the suite's stands in for it) is back in the server's own group after boot's layout, and so is the checkout's link to it (canary: the file's own group kept). `skill-mount.server.test.ts` "ruling 495(a)": under the server's umask, from a store folder at 0755 with 0700 folders and 0600 files, every folder of the plugin is 2775 (0775 where the platform gives no setgid bit), every file 0644 and a script 0755, and the store is unchanged (canaries: `cpSync` back; a file's mode not set on its descriptor); and through a `skills/` swapped for a link to a private folder of the server's, the copy stops at the folder already there and leaves its modes and contents as they were (canaries: a folder taken with `recursive` and chmod'ed after; `cpSync` back). `agent-reply.server.test.ts` "ruling 495(a)": the resume's workspace is handed to the agents' group before anything is made in it. The refusal the suite sees is logged while `support/` is not there yet, and where the hand-over lands `support/` carries the agents' group and setgid (canaries: the hand-over dropped; `support/<profileId>` made first, which the test's first version let pass). In the image, `scripts/check-agent-isolation.sh` gained twelve checks: the host kernel protects hard links and an agent cannot link a server file it cannot write; the server's `chmod -R -P` follows no link it is handed; the real mount (run with the image's `tsx` under the server's umask) leaves a plugin 2775 and group-readable, its person reads a skill file the store kept 0600 and removes the plugin with a plain `rm`; a plugin written the way the mount wrote one before this ruling resists the person's `rm` alone and is removed by `removeAgentTree`; an emptied workspace root no agent uid may unlink is removed by the server's `rmdir`; and the server opens and removes nothing through a folder an agent swapped for a link, whether the link is the agent's own or one of the server's that the agent moved there. Run against the e2e stack's container with the source changed there: without the chmod, the removal failed "EACCES on …/skills/sourced-content/SKILL.md" (F40-71's line); without the rmdir, "EACCES on …/WEB-2/workspace" (WEB-1's); without the link check, the server's steps removed the server-owned folder behind the link. After the review, the same way: with only links an agent uid owns flagged, the server's steps removed the server-owned folders behind a link of the server's own that an agent had moved ("the server acted through its own link an agent moved"); with `cpSync` back in the mount, the plugin's folders kept the store's modes (2755, and 2700 for its 0700 one) and its 0600 file, its person could neither read that file nor remove the plugin, and four checks failed. `npm run e2e` on the reviewed change (2026-09-26): the in-image check held 53 of 53, and Playwright passed 72 of 72 (52 of 52 and 72 of 72 before the review). (`app/server/runtimes/agent-trees.server.ts`, `agent-isolation.server.ts`, `skill-mount.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/agent-reply.server.ts`, `scripts/check-agent-isolation.sh`.)

496. **A pass over an unchanged GitHub writes nothing: a refusal keeps the time it was first seen, and the PR record is built in the order its file is read** (owner, 2026-09-26, pass 40, F40-72; spec `planning/discovery-2026-09-24-pass40-akinozer-site/SPEC-496.md`; dated note on ruling 360). Measured live on WEB-12 (deploy 10, PR #15 open from 23:12Z to 00:40Z on 2026-09-25/26): akin-ozer/website's credential has no `checks:read`, so GitHub refuses every check-runs read with 403, and the reconciler built `checksUnread: {status, message, at: new Date()}` on every refused pass, carrying the cached record only through a pass that read nothing. The `{pr, github}` snapshot never compared equal to the file, so every five-minute poll rewrote task.md (only `checksUnread.at` moved), rebuilt the projection (every open page revalidated over SSE) and wrote a `github.reconcile` provenance row: 19 rows for WEB-12 in 80 minutes, where DG-3 records a poll only when it changed something. Ruling 491 had hidden the pill; the fact still churned. Decided: **(a)** *The same refusal on the same PR carries its first `at`.* The same refusal is the same PR number, the same `status` and the same `message` (`checksRefusal`, `github-reconciler.server.ts`); the pass keeps the cached record whole, so it writes nothing, and on a poll it adds no row. A refusal that changes (another status or message), a refusal on another PR (an adopted replacement included) or a read that succeeds writes as before, and a success still drops `checksUnread` (ruling 360). The `checks:read` violation is unchanged: opened once, resolved by a read that succeeds. **(b)** *No other key of the compared snapshot moves on its own.* Every key of `newPr` and `newGithub` was audited, by reading the code and by running every reconcile the GitHub, push, audit and task-action suites make twice and then a third time over the same fake GitHub, logging any third pass that still changed: before this ruling 29 did, each on `checksUnread.at` or on the key order below; after it, none. `number`, `state`, `title`, `checks` (its roll-up keys in the schema's order), `review`, `mergeable`, `mergeableAt` (the head sha it was measured on, not a clock), `paths` (read only when the head moved, ruling 236), `headSha`, `revisionDrift`, `unpushedRevision`, `bodyWritten`, `humanApproval` (its `at` is GitHub's `submitted_at`) and `reviewRelay` come from GitHub or the cache and are carried on an unchanged pass; `closure.at` is stamped on the transition into closed and carried while the PR stays closed (ruling 160); `commits` with their `pushed` stamps, `otherCommits` and `foreignHead` come from the compare, and `changed` and `unownedPr` from the PR. The one other churn was the order of the keys. The change test compares the built `pr` with the parsed file as text, the parse returns `prRefSchema`'s order, and the pass set `revisionDrift` before `headSha`, which the schema lists first, so every PR carrying a recorded drift (a base refresh's, an authored drift before any verdict, the one a closed PR carries, F21-17) compared unequal to its own file on every pass and churned exactly as WEB-12 did. `headSha` is now set first, and the build states the rule it follows. Outside the snapshot, every pass still writes its `github.reconcile.task` audit row by design (the "Checked" clock, F19-22), a refused read opens no second violation, and the review relay writes only when it relays something new. **(c)** *`at` means first seen.* The schema's comment, `PrChecksUnread`, the description of the controller's `get_github_state` (the one reader that sees `at`; no pill prints it since ruling 491), `file-formats.md` and `github-delivery.md` §6, which now also says what DG-3 leaves unwritten, say that `at` is when the refusal was first seen, not the last pass that met it. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored byte for byte and checked with `cmp`): `github-reconciler.server.test.ts` "ruling 496": the same 403 on two passes leaves task.md byte-identical, adds no row under `skipUnchangedProvenance` and keeps the first pass's `at` (canary: every refused pass stamped); another message, then another status, then a read that succeeds each write, with a new `at` or no record (canaries: the status compared alone; the message alone); an adopted PR's refusal with the same status and message is stamped anew (canary: the file's PR compared whatever its number); an open PR carrying every fact a pass measures compares equal to its own file (canary: `revisionDrift` set before `headSha`); a PR closed with a refused read keeps its closure and its refusal on the next pass (canaries: every refused pass stamped; the closure stamped on every pass). `controller-access.server.test.ts` "ruling 496": the description says what `at` is (canary: the clause dropped). (`app/server/github/github-reconciler.server.ts`, `app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts`, `app/shared/mapping/task.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`.)

497. **A notification opens the thing it is about, and a click on a row about the page already on screen still takes you there** (owner, 2026-09-26, on a bell screenshot from the akinozer.com board: "notification clicking doesn't always route to it's page"; asked, the owner chose that each notification opens its own page and, for a row about the page on screen, "it goes to that message location and highlights"). Measured on a dev copy: a click on a row navigated from every page that carries the bell, under a revalidation every 150 ms and with four tabs open; what failed was the destination. `notificationHref` derived every link from the row's project and task alone (B-FD6), so a row about the task already on screen navigated to the URL on screen and moved nothing (the screenshot: WEB-3 open, two WEB-3 proposals in the bell); a knowledge-base proposal opened its task, not the Proposals panel where it is promoted or dismissed (ruling 483); "GitHub sync is failing" and a goal chain's progress opened the board; and a row about a timeline event (a verdict such as "Approval noted, waiting on Fact Checker", a PR note, a release) opened the top of a page whose newest events sit under the head, the packet and the side rail. Decided: **(a)** *A row records where it opens.* `notifications.href`, nullable, is written by the notifier that knows the exact thing: the timeline event it announces (`taskEventLink`, `#event-<occurredAt>`; an event has no id of its own, its time is what the file and the projection both keep, and the first of the events sharing a time carries the anchor), the open packet (`taskDecisionLink`, `#decision`: an operator's packet, an agent's question, a deadlock escalation, a maintainer's decision), the pending recommendations (`taskRecommendationsLink`, `#recommendations`), a proposal's entry (`proposalLink`, `/controller#proposal-<id>`), the project's GitHub page (`projectGithubLink`) and a goal chain or its link's row (`goalLink`, the anchors of rulings 419(h) and 476(b)). A task notice names its subject (`TaskWatcherNotice.about`; `noticeHref` builds the link), and the anchors are spelled once, in `app/shared/page-anchors.ts`, for the page that renders them and the notifier that links to them. Every writer is wired: mentions (the comment's time, which every comment writer already passes), ownership (the `assign` event), verdicts, failed runs, delivery notes, dependency releases and dead dependencies, file leases, context conflicts, scope violations, the reconciler's collision, conflict, drift, divergence, reopen and adoption notes, the restart note, packets, recommendations, proposals, the GitHub-sync alert and every goal notice. A notice with nothing to point at (the merge-pending nudge; a scope violation whose task file is gone) opens the task as before, and so do rows written before this ruling. **(b)** *Only inside its own project.* `notificationHref` uses a stored link only when it is the row's project page or under it, so the orphan rule (F18-1) and a member's removal still decide whether a row opens at all; any other link falls back to the task or the board the row names. **(c)** *The page takes you there, on every click.* The task page marks and focuses the event (`data-targeted`: a wash behind the entry with an outline, which forced colours keep), opens the filter tab that hid it, and loads older events (`?events=`, the hash kept) until the event is among them or the loaded timeline reaches past its time, each step once per navigation so the person can change tabs after; the packet and the recommendation cards are ringed and focused; the Controller page marks a proposal's entry (a router `pushState` never updates `:target`) and falls back to the panel for one promoted or dismissed since; goal links keep ruling 476(b)'s behaviour. One hook, `useHashTarget` (`app/ui/use-hash-target.ts`), reveals once per navigation keyed on the location, so a second click on a row about the page on screen, a new location with the same hash, brings the place back into view; only the nearest scroller moves (`revealTarget`, ruling 419(h)'s rule, now shared), and the task page's own focus on `.detail` (G7) no longer takes the focus back from an event its timeline revealed first. The hash is read only after hydration (`useHydrated`): a browser never sends it, so a document load of a link (a refresh, a pasted URL, the router's reload after a deploy) is rendered by the server with no mark, and hydration does not patch an attribute. **(d)** *The task page's document no longer scrolls.* A visually hidden heading in `.detail`, which was not positioned, sat at its place in the page's full height and made the document 152 px taller than a 1024×768 window, so any `scrollIntoView` on the page (the router's hash scroll, the composer's Ask operator) moved the shell up past its top bar with nothing to scroll it back. `.detail` is now the containing block of what it scrolls. **(e)** *Deployed roots gain the column when the database opens.* `href` is in `BASELINE_COLUMNS` (`ensureBaselineColumns`, `sqlite.server.ts`), the healer for additive columns on app-owned tables: `createNotification` names it on every insert and its callers fail open, so a root without it would drop every notification without a word. No backfill: NULL opens the task or the board, as every older row did. Tests (each red by canary, the source restored): `notifications.server.test.ts` "ruling 497" (each link opens; a foreign, a lookalike and an off-site link fall back to the task; a project that is gone opens nothing; the desktop notification opens where the row does), `sqlite.server.test.ts` "ensureBaselineColumns" (a root without the column gains it, its rows reading NULL), the writers in `task-mutation.server.test.ts` (ownership), `mention-notify.server.test.ts`, `agent-completion-notify.server.test.ts` (the verdict and its report), `agent-completion.server.test.ts` (a failed run), `operator-actions.server.test.ts` (packet, recommendation, proposal), `dependencies.server.test.ts`, `goal-actions.server.test.ts` (a link's row) and `reconcile-poller.server.test.ts` (the GitHub page), `timeline-target.test.tsx` (marked and focused; the hiding tab opened once; older events loaded with the hash kept; no loading past the event's time; a second click reveals again), `task-disposition.test.tsx` "ruling 497" (`#decision`, `#recommendations`, an event keeps its focus over G7), `hydration-determinism.test.tsx` (a link to an event hydrates with no warning and is marked after) and `controller-page.test.tsx` "ruling 497" (a proposal's entry; the panel for a closed one). Verified in a browser on the dev copy: from VIB-160 the release row opened VIB-148 with its note 8 px under the top, marked and focused; clicked again from VIB-148 scrolled to the top, it came back. *(Narrowed 2026-09-26 by ruling 503: `goalLink` became `epicLink`, the epic's page, and the notices an inbox held for a goal were re-pointed at its epic by the conversion.)* *(Narrowed 2026-09-27 by ruling 523: the mark lasts until the person's next press or key, which takes the hash out of the URL without a reload; the event a link focused keeps its tabindex after the mark, and a Controller page entry is marked by `data-targeted` alone.)* *(Extended 2026-09-28 by ruling 547: a decision's link names its packet (`#decision-<id>`) and moves to the entry that closed it once it closes; the reveal holds the place while the page settles; a link to a place the page no longer shows lands on the timeline.)*

498. **An agent's knowledge-base correction is written into the document as it is made, and a person undoes the ones they disagree with** (owner, 2026-09-26, on the Platform Engineer's proposal `kp-7de6ef2d03` on WEB-3's timeline, which corrected the deploy runbook's "That connection does not exist yet" from Workers Builds reads: "proposal spam is exhausting, it should be easier to get them merged to the kb. No human can approve all of these while inspecting them thoroughly." Asked how corrections should reach a knowledge base, the owner chose "Auto-merge, undo after" over keeping the project's rulings behind a one-click accept and over keeping proposals with a batch review by the controller. This reverses rulings 378 and 483 in part: "an agent proposes, a person promotes" becomes "an agent corrects, a person undoes"). The proposal the owner was reading is the shape those rulings gave every correction: a long timeline card ("Not binding until a person promotes it: …", the correction, the line and the evidence), a bell notification to every watcher of the task, a line in the controller's next turn saying it waits, and an entry on the project Controller page whose Promote cost a controller turn that re-read the document and composed the settled text. A review nobody can do thoroughly is a rubber stamp with a delay, and until the stamp came every run read the stale line as settled truth with the correction beside it. Decided: **(a)** *The door.* `propose_kb_correction` becomes `correct_knowledge_doc {kb?, doc, replaces?, text, evidence}` on the operator (the Claude tool, and the Codex plan action with `kbSource` `<kb>/<doc>`, `reason` the passage, `text` the text and `repoSource` the evidence; gate `append-typed-events`, as before) and on a Claude specialist with a knowledge base (gated on the grant, as before). `correctKnowledgeDoc` (`app/server/tasks/kb-correction-actions.server.ts`, renamed from `kb-proposal-actions.server.ts`) keeps ruling 483's reach (any knowledge base a run on the task was given; `kb` omitted means the rulings) and its refusals, and `mergeKbCorrection` (`app/server/org/kb-corrections.server.ts`) writes the document under the per-document lock: `replaces` must stand exactly once in the settled text (an unmerged proposals section is masked out of it, index for index), `text` takes its place, or goes at the end after a blank line when `replaces` is omitted (ruling 418's missing convention), in the document's own line endings and built by slicing, so `$$` and `$&` stay literal; `text` must stand exactly once afterwards, so an undo can find it; each side is at most 8 KB (`KB_CORRECTION_MAX_BYTES`, UTF-8 bytes, ruling 466); a document that already says it is a `noop`; a passage that is not there exactly is refused with the document's closest lines handed back verbatim in a fence (`fenceFor`, moved to `app/shared/text/fence.ts`, its test with it). Ruling 483 compared a quoted line loosely because it only anchored a note; a write needs the exact passage, and the refusal shows the agent what the document says. The Codex specialist's note asks for the passage exactly as the document has it; the operator skill (`viberr-app-expertise`, outgoing hash recorded), the operator's turn instructions (ruling 418's two sentences and ruling 483's relay), the specialist notes and every tool description say the correction is written at once and a person undoes it. **(b)** *The record and the undo.* The record is the audit row `task.kb_correction.merged` {id (`kc-` and ten hex characters), kb, doc, rulings, replaced, text, evidence (clipped to 4,000 characters), filedBy, actorRef, bytes}, subject the task. Nothing marks the document and no table is added, so no deployment re-baselines its projection. `undoKbCorrection` puts `replaced` back in place of `text` (or removes an addition with the blank line before it) while `text` still stands once, and refuses a document edited since, writing nothing; it records `task.kb_correction.undone` {id, kb, doc, reason, byName}, and `undoKbCorrectionOnTask` notes the undo on the task that made the correction ("Knowledge-base correction undone", as the person, with the reason). An agent that tries to write the same text into that document again is refused, naming who undid it and why: it puts its evidence to a person instead of re-filing. Audit retention (`AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`, 90) bounds how long a correction is listed and undoable; the document stays editable by hand after that. **(c)** *What people see.* A correction is one `kb_correction` event on the task (a thirteenth timeline type, pilled "Knowledge base" in the proposal's tint and glyph), titled "Knowledge base corrected" or "Rulings corrected", whose text is the document, the id and two list items, `**Was:** ~~…~~` and `**Now:** …`, each clipped to one line; an agent's links "Review or undo" to the Controller page. Nobody is notified: nothing is owed, and the bell is where a person finds what is. The project Controller page's Proposals panel becomes the **Knowledge base** panel (`knowledge-panel.tsx`, loader `projectCorrections`): the newest 20 corrections with the count on record, each with its passages, collapsed evidence, task, filer, time and id, and for an org admin Undo (confirmed, with an optional reason) and Open document. Undo posts `kb-correction-undo` to the project controller route, which undoes directly for an org admin (403 otherwise): an undo is the recorded edit in reverse, with nothing to compose, so it costs no controller turn. The controller gets `undo_kb_correction {id, projectSlug?, reason}` (org admin, when a person asks) and `get_project.kbCorrections`, the controller guide says so (outgoing hash recorded), and a reply naming a `kc-` id links to its entry; a link to an entry (`#correction-<id>`, `correctionAnchor` beside ruling 497's anchors in `app/shared/page-anchors.ts`) marks and focuses it the way ruling 497 reveals a notification's target, and one the panel no longer lists leaves the panel in view. **(d)** *The proposals already filed.* Nothing files a proposal now (`fileKbProposal` and its formatting helpers are gone); documents keep theirs, which every run still reads beside the line, and ruling 483's reader, context lines (now saying they predate this ruling), `openProposals`, `resolve_kb_proposal`, Promote and Dismiss stay for them, listed under the corrections, with **Promote all**, which asks the controller once for the lot (`promoteAllRequest`). Not changed: who may read a knowledge base, the rulings knowledge base's binding line (ruling 286), and the three always-human capabilities. Budgets (ruling 457), raised to the measured values with the reason beside each when main (carrying ruling 497) was merged in: gzip closures `root` +55 B (the `kb_correction` type in the schema every route bundles, and root.css +46 B for the activity tint, a correction's two sides and its evidence fold, which shares `.ctl-goal-more`'s summary rules rather than copying them), `routes/login` +61, `routes/_index` +63, `routes/project.board` +56, `routes/profile` +57, `routes/project.task` +167 (plus the type's meta and the timeline's "Review or undo" link), `routes/controller` +1,139 (the Knowledge base panel lives in the controller page module both controller routes share, and `routes/project.controller`, unbudgeted, carries the same panel). Tests: `kb-corrections.server.test.ts` (the exact passage replaced and both sides kept on the record for its board; an addition before a proposals section; a passage not there exactly, with its closest line handed back and nothing written; a passage only an entry quotes; a passage twice before and a text twice after; a document the base does not hold; nothing to write; `$&`, `$$` and CRLF; the cap; a nested document; an undo put back, recorded and refused a second time; an addition undone; an edited document refused; another board's id; the refused re-filing), `kb-proposals.server.test.ts` (the reader and the closer, on documents built as the filing left them, `test-support/kb-legacy-proposals.ts`), `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "rulings 378, 483 and 498" (the write, the one short entry, the audit and no notification; an engaged agent's base; a stranger's base and an inexact passage; UTF-8 bytes; `$`, an addition and the second `noop`; no rulings KB and a mistyped document; the missing fields and the denied capability), `agent-toolkit.server.test.ts` "rulings 483 and 498", `operator-run.server.test.ts` (ruling 418's sentences, the relay, the Codex plan's `<kb>/<doc>` and passage, the fallback list), `specialist-run.server.test.ts` "rulings 483 and 498", `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 498" (`kbCorrections`; the undo, org admins only, its note on the task, a second undo), `controller-query.server.test.ts` "ruling 498", `controller-page.test.tsx` "ruling 498" (the list, the Undo, a correction's link marked and focused) and "ruling 483" (the proposals under the Knowledge base panel, Promote all, and ruling 497's notification target, whose closed entry now lands on the proposals list), `routes/controller.test.ts` "ruling 498" (a member's 403), `task-detail-components.test.tsx` (the thirteen types; both links), `markdown.test.tsx` (a `kc-` id), `default-assets.server.test.ts` "ruling 498" (the outgoing hashes). Each red by canary against its source, restored byte for byte: the settled view unmasked, the undo's count check loosened, the re-filing guard off, the project filter off, the event written as a `proposal`, `kbCorrections` renamed, the Undo sent as a `send`, the route's org-admin check off, the timeline link narrowed to proposals, the skill's outgoing hash dropped, the specialist tool renamed, and the Codex plan's passage dropped. *(Narrowed 2026-09-28 by ruling 568: the task's entry quotes the passage only for the project's rulings or a knowledge base every deployed specialist is given.)*

499. **The run console draws what an agent did the way agent tools draw it: an edit as its diff, a to-do list as its steps, a thought as a thinking block, output as a code block, a wait as an orb** (owner, 2026-09-26, of an `Edit` row on WEB-3, `tool_use  [Edit] /data/projects/akinozer-com/tasks/WEB-3/workspace/website/docs/deploy-runbook.md · + old_string, new_string`: "this diff looks dated design find out in the internet what people does and let's make it coherent with the app as well", then, the same hour, "let's implement these components: https://www.aicss.dev/#components"). Measured: an edit's row printed the host path of the task's checkout and ruling 366(d)'s link, which opened the replaced text and its replacement as two plain rows one above the other; a `TodoWrite` row printed `todos: [5 items]` and `+ todos (5 items)`; a Codex `todo_list` item printed an empty `meta` row, because the projection kept none of its steps; the thought fold, the output block and the wait row's canvas orb were each styled on their own. A survey of how agent tools draw an edit in 2025–2026 (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Zed, Roo Code; `@pierre/diffs`, `react-diff-view`, `diff2html`, Monaco; Primer's diff colours) found one shape nearly everywhere: the file's name with a green `+N` and a red `−M`, the diff inline and unified, removed and added lines in muted tints with the changed words in a stronger one, the `+`/`−` beside the colour, about three unchanged lines around each change with the rest folded behind a count, and a bounded height that opens on demand. AICSS offers sixteen components: ten are free under MIT (`@aicss/react` 0.1.3, "Copyright (c) 2026 AICSS") and six are Pro, their code licensed and not public. Decided: **(a)** *An edit is its diff* (`editDiff`, `app/features/runtime/edit-diff.ts`, over `diffSteps` and `changedSpans`, `app/shared/line-diff.ts`). `diffSteps` is Myers' O(ND) difference after matching the common head and tail (an edit quotes the lines around its change, so that is most of it); past 1,000 steps or 6,000 lines it reads the change as every old line removed and every new one added, a true account that is only not the shortest. `changedSpans` marks the changed words of a removed line and the added line paired with it, joined across spaces, and marks none when the two keep less than half their characters (a rewrite, not an edit). `Edit`, `MultiEdit` (each edit under its own "edit N of M" marker, with "every occurrence" where it applies) and `Write` are drawn; a change's removed lines come before its added ones; three unchanged lines stay on each side of a change and a longer run folds behind "N unchanged lines", which opens in place (never a fold of one line). What the record does not carry is not drawn: an edit names strings, not places, so its lines have no numbers; a `Write`'s lines are numbered, since they are the whole file, and it claims no `+N −M`, because the record holds no earlier file. The row prints the file repo-relative (`normalizeWorkspacePaths`, moved from `agent-reply.server.ts` to `app/shared/workspace-paths.ts`, the F7-UX1 rewrite the timeline already applies), the folder quiet and the name plain, the path the call named on hover, then `+N −M` (read to assistive tech as "added, … removed") or a `Write`'s line count. Under it the diff sits in a card: its first ten rows, and past twelve the rest behind "Show N more lines", which is the row's own disclosure, so the console's re-folding keeps it open. `hiddenArguments` takes the arguments a row draws in full and names none of them, so `+ old_string, new_string` is gone; a row whose summary IS its `file_path` (a `Read`: `filePathOf`) prints repo-relative too, and a path inside a command is never rewritten, since that would change what the command says. **(b)** *A to-do list is its steps* (AICSS To-do List; `consoleTodos`, `console-todos.ts`; `TodoCard`, `console-blocks.tsx`). Claude's `TodoWrite` input is read as it stands; a Codex `todo_list` item's steps now ride its completed line as `LogLine.todos` (the plan as the turn left it; a Codex step is done or waiting, and names no step in progress). The card's header carries the list's progress, a wedge inside a dotted ring (a green check once every step is done), "To-dos" and "2/5"; the chevron shows on hover and the header folds the list. Each step carries its mark (a dotted ring waiting, an arrow in the ring under way, a check done, struck through) and its status in words for assistive tech. The step under way shimmers only while the run is live and the list is the one the agent wrote last (`latestTodoRow`); an older list, or a finished run's, holds still. **(c)** *A thought is a thinking block* (AICSS Thinking + Reasoning and Thinking State): the fold reads "Thought for 4s · 2 steps", the verb above the figure, with a chevron that turns as it opens; while the run is live and the fold is its last row, "Thinking" shimmers (the controller's working line's band, ruling 451(a), in the console's ink). **(d)** *Output is a code block* (AICSS Code Block): a head with the terminal glyph, what it holds and its size ("Output · 8 lines") and Copy, now carrying the copy mark as every other copy control does; the lines numbered in a gutter that assistive tech and the selection skip; still bounded and scrolling, never cut. Code in the diff and the block draws no ligatures, so `!==` reads as typed. **(e)** *A wait is an orb* (AICSS Orbs, the lattice): nine CSS dots, a pulse radiating from the centre while a tool runs and a comet round the ring on a Viberr tool, in its chip's lavender; the dots stop once the wait ends and hold the centre lit under reduced motion. `thinking-orbs` is removed, with the canvas stub `setup-dom.ts` kept for it. **(f)** *One card.* The diff, the to-do list and the code block share one card a shade above the console (`#131823`, a `#262d3d` hairline, `--radius-box`, a soft shadow), in literal hex like every console rule, and the contrast gate measures the thinking block and the orb on the console's fill (`RENDERED_INSIDE`). The adapted design is credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` with AICSS's MIT licence. **(g)** *Not taken.* None of AICSS's six Pro components (File Diff, Reasoning Effort, Inline Citations, Comparison Table, Audio Waves, Image Processing) is recreated: their licence reserves the code, and the diff above is the app's own, the Changes panel's rows (ruling 484) in the console's colours. Streaming Text is not taken either: Viberr streams no tokens (ruling 451's sweep said the same). The components the task page can take (Approval Card, AI Agent Input, Data Table, Code Block, Text Response) are ruling 500's. This narrows ruling 366 (the canvas orb; `+ old_string, new_string` and `+ todos (N items)`, which the rows now draw) and ruling 451(c) (the console's word-only copy control). Stored lines are not reprojected: a Codex plan written before this ruling keeps its empty row. Budgets (ruling 457): `bundle:root.css` +1,350 B gzip (the blocks' rules; `app.css` is one stylesheet), so every route closure +1,388 to +1,392 B (the rules and the to-do list's two glyphs in the shell's icon set, `todo` and `todonow`); `routes/project.task` −1,124 B and `routes/controller` −1,116 B net, because the `thinking-orbs` canvas library left the console's closure (ceilings raised and lowered to the measured figures, the reasons beside them); `render:css.main-thread-infinite-loops` 1 → 3, the two live shimmers (the orb's dots animate opacity and transform only, its easing on the animation rather than inside its keyframes).
