It is streaming to the agent logs." **(b)** *What read the old text reads both.* `closureRefusal` (ruling 177) is now `closureClaim`, what is true of the closed task, followed by its remedy: "<KEY> is archived. Restore it before <verb>." and "<KEY> is closed (<Stage> is the terminal stage). Move it back to an open stage before <verb>."; the note for a run that finished after its task closed takes the claim, where it used to cut the refusal at its dash. The activity feed's forced-acceptance reader still splits a row recorded before this ruling at its dash, and a newer one at its first sentence. A decision written into the goal joins the option's title and detail with a colon, and O39-b reads a dash in a decision the goal already holds as that colon, so a goal written before this ruling is not given the same decision twice. **(c)** *One exemption.* `EVIDENCE_EMPTY_COLUMN`, the "—" that task.md holds for an evidence row with no result, is a format glyph the parser reads back as empty, and the page never shows it. **(d)** *The gate.* `copy-ban.test.ts` scans every string literal under the four roots and in `app/routes.ts` with the govern literal test's lexer, so comments and regular expressions stay free, against a one-entry allowlist that fails when an entry matches nothing. The dash pattern of all three of its dash scans now reads the escaped spellings too (`\u2014`, `\u{2014}`, `&mdash;` and the numeric entities): the sweep found escapes in the operator's and the controller's prompts and tool descriptions, and an `&mdash;` in the decision card's duplicate-task note, which the character-only scan had passed since P21. Not changed: comments, tests and the docs' own prose keep their dashes, and rulings before this one quote the wording of their day; what the model writes is still ruling 502's to shape; the hyphen, the minus sign and arrows stay legal. A report an agent repeats word for word across the deploy compares unequal once where a server-written disclosure rides it, so the operator reacts to it one extra time. Tests: `copy-ban.test.ts` "no string literal under app/server, app/schemas, app/shared or app/lib carries one (ruling 571)" (canary: the dash back in `runDispatchLine`'s started tail; with an `\u2014` escape restored in `agent-reply.server.ts` and the `&mdash;` restored in `decision-packet.tsx`, the literal and render scans name both); `task-governance.server.test.ts` "ruling 571: a decision the goal holds from before, joined with a dash, is not written again" (canary: compare the stored answer without reading its dash as the colon, and the goal holds the decision twice); `task-closure.server.test.ts`, and the closure refusals the schedule, relay, dispatch and mention tests quote. Budgets (ruling 457): the reworded strings of the shared and schema modules and the card's note grew the board closure 6 B (256,724 -> 256,730), the task page's 19 B (331,963 -> 331,982), the Controller's 10 B (279,579 -> 279,589) and the Profile's 2 B (212,321 -> 212,323), each ceiling raised with its note; the task page's and the Controller's also carry the 41 B and 40 B that PR #396 (ruling 564) added on main without moving them. (`app/features/copy-ban.test.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-closure.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/projections/activity-feed.server.ts`, `app/features/task-detail/decision-packet.tsx`, `docs/ui/surfaces.md`, `docs/development/testing.md`, `docs/domain/agents-and-runtime.md`, `docs/domain/task-lifecycle.md`, `docs/domain/controller-and-epics.md`, `docs/domain/github-delivery.md`, `docs/operations/runbook.md`, `test-support/perf-budgets/bundle.json`.)

572. **The controller transcript reads as one column, and a reader who scrolled away has a way back to the newest message** (owner, 2026-09-28: "look at this carefully and find ways of implementing some of this to viberr. Compare with screenshots assess etc.", on https://github.com/shadcn-ui/chatbot-template; design calls made in an unattended run, marked for the owner to revisit; extends rulings 419(d) and 476(c)). The template is a minimal chat app (Next.js, the AI SDK, shadcn/ui and `@shadcn/react`'s message scroller, questionnaire and typeset). It was read as a design reference, never installed (ruling 166), and compared on screenshots of both apps at 1440×900 and 390×844, Viberr's on a seeded eight-message instance thread and the template's on a mocked stream. Most of what it shows Viberr already had: example asks that send on click (ruling 314), a shimmer on the working sentence (ruling 451(a)), a code block with its language and Copy (ruling 500), a composer that grows with what is typed, and a transcript that never scrolls the page under it. It did two things Viberr did not. **(a)** *The jump back.* The template's scroller carries a button, shown while the reader is away from the end, that takes them there. Ruling 476(c) leaves a reader in history where they are when a reply lands, and only a screen reader was told that one had (476(d)); a thread measured 12,625px on a phone, and the wheel was the only way back. Both transcripts now end in `TranscriptJumpButton` (`app/features/controller/transcript-jump.tsx`), fed by `useTranscriptFollow`, which remembers the reply it left below a reader in history. The jump says "New reply" on the primary face then, and puts that reply's first line at the top of the box; otherwise it says "Latest" and goes where opening the thread would (the newest reply's first line when a reply is the newest message, else the end). It shows only while that place sits below what the reader can see, less a line (32px), so a thread opened on its newest reply shows none; a held reply the reader scrolls to counts as read, and the jump falls back to Latest or leaves. It is pinned to its box's foot in a sticky row of no height, so the box's end holds still as it comes and goes; it enters as a message does (`dock-msg-in`, a fade under reduced motion); and it hands the focus it held to the message it showed (`tabIndex=-1`, no scroll), since it leaves as that message comes into view. The hook measures after every placement and on the box's own scroll, once a frame. **(b)** *One reading column.* The template sets a 42rem column in the middle of the page: the person's messages are bubbles at its end, and a reply is text on the page. Viberr's replies were agent-tinted cards inside the transcript's own card, at the start of a 1,092px desktop transcript, and the person's messages stood at its far end (right edge at 1,101px of a 1,440px window). The thread is now one column, 48rem at most and centred (`.ctl-msgs`); the person's message keeps its bubble, 92% of the column at most, at its end (right edge at 955px); a reply has no frame (`.ctl-msg.from-controller`: no border, no padding, the column's width) under the header that names who wrote it. Ruling 419(d)'s frame inside a frame goes at every width: a reply's text is 291px wide on a 375px phone (273 before), 364px in the dock (338) and 768px on a desktop (707), and the phone's transcript keeps a .75rem gutter where it had .5rem. The dock's thread keeps a step less air than the page's (1rem between messages against 1.25rem). Not taken, and why: Enter to send (every composer that takes more than a line sends on ⌘/Ctrl+Enter, the controller's included, and its messages are instructions a person means to finish); the model picker (the controller's model is its profile's, set by an org admin); syntax colours in a reply's code (ruling 500 renders a comment's block at once and leaves the grammars to the reader); streamed tokens (a turn's reply lands whole, and ruling 451 turned down streaming text); a fade at the transcript's foot (it would fade the jump, and a mask clips focus rings); the `d` key for dark mode (a single-character shortcut, which WCAG 2.1.4 wants a way to turn off); the questionnaire and the sources drawer (the controller would have to offer structured choices or citations, a toolkit and storage change for a ruling of its own). Tests: `controller-page.test.tsx` "ruling 572" (Latest is never shown to a reader on the newest reply, is shown above it and goes where an open goes; New reply when one lands on a reader in history, taking them and the focus to its first line; no longer said once they scroll to it), `controller-dock.test.tsx` "(ruling 572)" (the dock offers the same jump), `app.css.test.ts` "ruling 572" ((b) the centred column, the bubble, and no frame on a reply at any width or preference; (a) the sticky row of no height and its reduced-motion fade). Canaries, each run: drop the box's scroll listener; measure against the box's end instead of the newest reply; forget the reply left below the reader; drop the focus move; hold the reply until the jump is pressed; drop the dock's jump; frame a reply in any `@media` rule; drop the row's `height: 0`.

573. **A person's files go with what they say, in every chat** (owner, 2026-09-28: "I want file upload to every chat sections possible", and, offered ReUI's and shadcn's ready-made attachment components, "Rebuild them in Viberr"; extends rulings 527 and 533, amends 533(a)'s single-surface Files field into a shared tray). A person could hand a file to a task's attachments panel (ruling 379) or file a task with it (ruling 533), and nowhere else: the controller page, the controller dock and a task's comment composer took words only, so a screenshot of a portal or an inventory export reached the controller as a description of it. ReUI's composer tray (`c-attachment-2`), its file-in-reply (`c-attachment-1`) and upload states (`c-attachment-5`), its `use-file-upload` hook, shadcn's `Attachment` and the AI Elements prompt input were read as design references and rebuilt in Viberr's own code and stylesheet, never installed (ruling 166). Decided: **(a)** *One tray, three composers.* `app/ui/attach-files.tsx` draws a composer's files: a paperclip that opens the picker (a button beside a hidden input, so the press is the button's own, ruling 459), a tray of chips over the text (a picture's own thumbnail or the file glyph, the name, the size, a remove button), a drop on the composer's frame (dashed while files are held over it) and a pasted screenshot (a paste that carries text stays text, 533(a)'s rule). `app/ui/picked-files.ts` holds the rules the tray keeps files by, the upload's own (the kinds Viberr stores, 10 MB each, at most ten and 25 MB together, a file picked again under one name replacing the first), shared with the New task dialog, whose bundle carries the rules and not the tray. The server refuses the same batch in the same words (`checkAttachmentBatch`, with `MESSAGE_BATCH` or `FILING_BATCH`, `attachment-kinds.ts`). Files alone are a message. Each composer clears a file only once the server took it, as ruling 259 clears the words. **(b)** *A controller message carries files.* They are stored with the message in SQLite (`controller_message_files`, a BLOB per file), so a backup carries them, a message and its files commit together, a retracted message takes its files with it and a deleted conversation takes all of them. The send doors check them before any thread is created (U35-4's rule); a first message of files alone is titled by their names. The turn that reads the message is told what came, by name and size, and to read each with `read_message_file`, the controller's 58th tool: one file of THIS conversation by name, with the task reader's rules (text, an `.xlsx` as CSV, an image as the picture, pages of 40,000 characters, `readAttachmentContent`). A steering or queued message is told the same when its turn reads it, and the recent exchange lists what earlier messages carried. The transcript shows a message's files under its words, on the page and in the dock (`message-files.tsx`): a picture as itself in a frame sized before it loads, any other file as the tray's chip, each opening from `/resources/controller-file/:id`, which serves the conversation's owner and a live org admin (the two who may read the transcript) and 404s anyone else, with the task route's `nosniff`, sandbox CSP and inline whitelist. Retract (ruling 527) reads a message's files back before it takes the message back and puts them in the tray with its words; if they cannot be read, nothing is retracted. **(c)** *A task comment carries files.* For whoever may attach one (`attach-file`, a task not archived, the panel's own rule), the comment's files land as the task's attachments inside the claim that keeps a completing run from taking them (ruling 558), the comment claims them (`attachments:`, 533(b)) so the timeline draws them under it and the panel says who added them, each is audited `task.attachment.added`, and the comment's text names them, so the agent it wakes and every other reader learns what came. A refused file refuses the comment with nothing written, and no name an agent run saved is replaced (ruling 388). Tests: `resources.controller.test.ts` "ruling 573: files sent with a controller message" (a refused file makes no thread; files alone stored, titled, named to the turn, served to the owner and 404 to another member; Retract hands back the words alone and the files leave with the message), `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 573: read_message_file" (this conversation's file only, the names it holds otherwise), `controller-run.server.test.ts` "ruling 573: the turn is told what files came" (a steering message), `controller-dock.test.tsx` "ruling 573: files from the dock" (a tray sent as a multipart form with no words and emptied on success, kept on failure, a refusal said), `controller-page.test.tsx` "ruling 573: files on the controller page", `task-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 573: a comment with files", `comment-files.test.tsx` and `picked-files.test.ts`. Canaries, each seen red and restored: the dock's file append dropped; the files note left out of a turn's start and out of `steeringText`; the send door's check dropped (an empty thread is made); the comment's `attachments` left off its event; the comment composer's paste capture dropped. (`app/ui/attach-files.tsx`, `app/ui/picked-files.ts`, `app/features/controller/controller-page.tsx`, `app/features/controller/controller-dock.tsx`, `app/features/controller/controller-dock-panel.tsx`, `app/features/controller/message-files.tsx`, `app/features/controller/waiting-actions.tsx`, `app/features/task-detail/timeline.tsx`, `app/routes/resources.controller-file.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-conversations.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-run.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/files/task-attachments.server.ts`, `app/server/files/form-files.server.ts`, `db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql`.)

574. **A person may attach a file of any kind; its size is the limit** (owner, 2026-09-28: "we should support every file type except for big files of course, file extensions doesnt matter since agents will read it"; reverses ruling 379's upload whitelist and the extension refusals of rulings 533 and 573; extends ruling 363's text test to the coordinators' readers). Ruling 379 stored only what Viberr could render inline or read back as text, on the reasoning that anything else was a blob and would make the panel a file manager. But a file a person attaches is for the agents on the task, which read the attachments folder whatever the names in it, and the whitelist refused exactly the inputs a customer hands over: a `.tf`, a `.ps1`, a `.docx`, a `Dockerfile`, a zip of configs. Decided: **(a)** *Any kind is stored.* `checkAttachmentUpload` no longer checks the extension, and `UPLOADABLE_EXTENSIONS` is gone; the pickers (the attachments panel, the New task dialog, the chat tray) offer any file. What still refuses an upload: a name that is empty, starts with a dot or is not one path segment, a file over 10 MB (`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`), and a batch past 10 files or 25 MB (rulings 533, 573). **(b)** *Serving is unchanged, and is what keeps a stored page inert.* `INLINE_TYPES` (images, PDF and the inert text types, never `.html`, `.svg` or `.js`) is still the only list the serving routes render inline; every other kind is an `application/octet-stream` download under `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP, as an agent's own files of any kind always were. **(c)** *The readers read by the bytes.* `read_task_attachment` and `read_message_file` read an `.xlsx` as CSV and an image as the picture, as before, and any other file as text unless it names a known binary kind (`BINARY_EXTENSIONS`, moved from the task page's viewer to `app/shared/attachment-kinds.ts` so both use one list) or its first 8,000 bytes hold a NUL (git's `-text` test, ruling 363's). A binary file is named with what the reader takes instead, never guessed at. Tests: `task-attachments.server.test.ts` "ruling 574: stores a file of any kind, and serves one a browser could run only as a download" and "ruling 574: readTaskAttachment reads any text file" (a `.tf` read whole, a `.docx` named binary); the tests that pinned the old refusal now pin the refusals that remain (a file over the cap in `task-actions.server.test.ts`, `task-relay.server.test.ts`, `picked-files.test.ts`, `controller-dock.test.tsx` and `resources.controller.test.ts`; a dot-prefixed name in `task-detail-route.server.test.ts`; a picker with no `accept` in `attachments-panel.test.tsx`). Canaries, each seen red and restored: an extension check put back in `checkAttachmentUpload`; the text read gated on `READABLE_TEXT_EXTENSIONS` again. (`app/shared/attachment-kinds.ts`, `app/server/files/task-attachments.server.ts`, `app/ui/picked-files.ts`, `app/ui/attach-files.tsx`, `app/features/board/filed-files.tsx`, `app/features/task-detail/attachments-panel.tsx`, `app/features/task-detail/attachment-kind.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`.)

575. **The controller is told that a required reviewer never delivers** (AWSC-11, 2026-09-28; extends ruling 556). Planning round 2 of the AWS calculator board, the controller wrote "Benchmark task: the Estimate Judge delivers" into AWSC-11's goal, on a board whose rule is "Estimate Judge reviews at Review", and told the owner to force-accept the task once the Judge had delivered, "just as with AWSC-3". AWSC-3 ran before ruling 556, which now refuses that hand-off, so the operator's first act on AWSC-11 was a decision packet asking the owner how the Judge should run. The controller had read `requiredReviewers` from `get_project`, but no tool it holds said what the rule means for a plan. Decided: `set_required_reviewers` says that the agent a rule names never delivers on the project, that work only it can do (such as correcting a knowledge base only it is granted) runs it as a supporting agent and closes when a project admin force-accepts it, and that the controller writes such a task's goal, and what it tells people about it, that way. `get_project`'s description now names `requiredReviewers` and points there. Test: `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 575: tells the planner the required reviewer never delivers, and how work only it can do runs" (canary: either sentence dropped). (`app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`.)

576. **A task that corrected a knowledge base did not complete "with no changes"** (AWSC-11, 2026-09-28; extends rulings 62, 498 and 556). The Estimate Judge, the AWS calculator board's required reviewer, is the only agent given the golden set, so ruling 556 left one way to correct its sample-01 entry: run it as a supporting agent. It wrote three corrections (ruling 498), saved two files and approved. Nothing went to the repository, so the task met R19-8's shape: the approval minted a verification of `main` and read "Estimate Judge approved: there is nothing to deliver … Accepting completes this task with no changes.", the operator's card offered "Complete AWSC-11 with no changes", the accept dialog said the same, and the permanent record reads "AWSC-11 completed with no changes. Nothing was delivered …", of a task whose whole outcome was the three corrections. Ruling 556 names such a record a defect. Decided: `standingKbCorrections` reads the corrections made on a task that nobody has undone, from the records the Controller page lists. With any, **(a)** the approval that verifies nothing goes to the repository says so, names them by id and document with who made them (never the passage, ruling 568), and, when the approving reviewer made every one, says the approval is not a review of them; **(b)** the operator's acceptance card offers to complete the task "with no repository changes" and names them; **(c)** every writer of the completion record (the Accept button, the packet door and the operator under full autonomy) titles it "Completed with no repository changes" and says "Its outcome is the knowledge-base corrections made on it, which stand: …". A task with none keeps its words. **(d)** The accept dialog's no-change row names no outcome: under "Merges" it says "Nothing." and the branch's state, and the auto-detect sentence says the task "closes with nothing merged". A first wording, "no repository changes", grew the board closure past its ceiling; this one shrank both (board 257,259 to 257,237 bytes, task 334,059 to 334,039, measured on main after ruling 574), and the ceilings moved down with them (ruling 457). **(e)** The Review note that the operator decides delivery (push + review PR) is not written on a task a reviewer verified has nothing to deliver, as ruling 546 already spares a task delivered as files: on AWSC-11 it followed that verification by 30 seconds. The mechanics are unchanged: the verification still binds the verdict, so the operator's completion packet, which needs a review subject, is still written, and a task that delivered nothing is still not held by its required reviewer (ruling 385). Tests: `no-change-acceptance.server.test.ts` "ruling 576: …" (the reviewer's own correction named on the note, the card and the record; the packet door and the operator under full autonomy; another agent's correction named without the "not a review" clause, and an undone one forgotten). `delivery-decision.server.test.ts` "ruling 576: no safety-net event for a task a reviewer verified has nothing to deliver". Canaries: the corrections dropped from the note, the card or any of the three writers; the "made every one" check dropped; the undone filter dropped; `noChangeApplies` dropped from the note's condition. (`app/server/tasks/no-change-completion.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts`, `app/features/task-detail/accept-confirm.tsx`.)

577. **No Claude run keeps Claude Code's auto-memory** (live, 2026-09-28; follows ruling 564). Ruling 564 gave a run that posts files its `Edit`, `MultiEdit` and `Write`, confined to the task's attachments folder and the temp directory. The CLI's auto-memory, on by default because Viberr passes `settingSources: []` and no setting turns it off, then told agents to keep notes in the account home (`claude-home/…/projects/<workspace>/memory/`). Between 12:00 and 23:50 UTC, 13 of 138 Claude runs tried: 32 writes, 29 refused by the hook and none kept, each refusal a turn spent. Before ruling 564 some did land, ten notes on round-1 tasks (a price-list fallback, a calculator form lesson), each readable only by the same agent on the same task, where a knowledge base would have taught every run on the board. Decided: every Claude run (operator, controller, specialist, and the completion compaction, which builds its options the same way) sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` over its base and per-run env, so the CLI neither prompts for memory nor loads it; a board learns through its knowledge bases (ruling 498). Test: `claude-runtime.server.test.ts` "is off on every run, over the base env and the run's own" (a specialist and an operator run; an ambient `0` is overridden; canary: the switch dropped). `harness-hermeticity.server.test.ts` names the key among those Viberr adds to a Claude run's child env (ruling 371), where it was caught unnamed. (`app/server/runtimes/claude-runtime.server.ts`.)

578. **A knowledge base can be private: its folder is the server's alone, and only the runs it is granted read it, through their knowledge tool** (AWSC-12, 2026-09-29; extends rulings 283, 422 and 460). Reviewing AWSC-12, the Estimate Judge found its own golden set, the benchmark's answer key and granted to it alone, world-readable on the host (folder 0775, files 0664). Measured in `viberr-app-1`: as uid 20001 in group `viberr-agents`, the identity every agent of the board's owner runs as, the answer key's README and AWSC-3's `golden-files.md` both read. Ruling 460(d) makes `kb/` readable to agents on purpose, and every agent of one person runs as that person's uid, so no file mode can keep one of them out of what another is given: a grant decides what a run is handed (its index, its `read_knowledge_doc`, ruling 422's read exception), never what its shell can open. Nothing in round 1 or 2 read the key (the runs' tool calls were checked), but the board's rulings promised a secrecy Viberr did not provide. Decided: **(a)** a knowledge base is private when its store folder grants nothing to its group or to others (0700); the flag is the folder's own mode (`isPrivateKbFolder`), so it needs no column, survives a backup, and the boot layout check, which sets `kb/` and never the folders inside it, cannot widen it. **(b)** `save_knowledge_base` takes `private` (org admin; `setKnowledgeBasePrivacy`, audited as `org.kb.privacy`), `list_knowledge_bases` and the Instance settings row show it ("private: only the runs it is granted read it"), and the tool's description says an open knowledge base is readable by every agent's shell, so an answer key goes into a private one. **(c)** A private knowledge base's index says so and sends the run to `read_knowledge_doc`, which the server answers; `knowledgeBaseReadDirs` leaves it out of the workspace contract; and a Codex specialist, which mounts no Viberr tools (ruling 422), gets it as an unresolved grant: "it is private (ruling 578): its folder is closed to every shell, and this run has no knowledge tool to read it". The operator and the controller read it through their own `read_knowledge_doc`. What stays open: a task's attachments are readable by every agent (the board's AWSC-3 still holds its first copy of the key), and `/tmp` (ruling 460(j)). Tests: `kb-injection.server.test.ts` "a private knowledge base (ruling 578)" (the mode, the index for a run with and without a knowledge tool); `specialist-run.server.test.ts` "ruling 578: knowledgeBaseReadDirs never names a private folder" and "ruling 578: a private KB reaches a Claude run through read_knowledge_doc, and a Codex run is told it cannot"; `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 578: private closes a knowledge base's folder …" (0700, the list, open again at 0755, the unchanged reply); `agent-isolation.server.test.ts` "ruling 578: never opens a private knowledge base"; `resource-rows.test.tsx` "a private knowledge base (ruling 578)". Canaries: the private sentence dropped, the no-tool miss dropped, the read-folder exclusion dropped, every backend handed the tool, the controller's privacy call dropped, the layout set to walk `kb/`, the row's branch dropped. (`app/server/files/kb-injection.server.ts`, `app/server/org/resources.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/specialist-run.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/features/org-settings/resource-rows.tsx`.) *(Completed 2026-09-29 by ruling 585: a Codex specialist reads a private knowledge base, and corrects it, through `viberr_knowledge`, a server Viberr's gateway answers itself; it gets the grant as unresolved only when the gateway is not running.)*

579. **Another task's goal is read with every decision recorded on it** (AWSC-16, 2026-09-29; extends rulings 189, 289 and 569). `read_board` with a key returns the first 2,000 characters of that task's goal (ruling 289), so a second task's contract does not compete with the reader's own prompt. But the decisions people write into a goal (ruling 189) are appended at its end, the part the cap cuts. Live on AWSC-16, the round-2 comparison read AWSC-15's goal, 2,751 characters, and the Workflow Researcher wrote that it "cannot say whether a third decision is recorded in the clipped tail". Decided: the cap applies to the goal's own text. The decision blocks `resolvePacket` appends (a rule, then "**Decision: <date>, <person> answered …", in either separator, since ruling 571 made the dash a colon) follow the excerpt whole, and the excerpt's marker says so: "Above are the first 2,000 of its own text, and every decision recorded on it follows, whole." A goal whose own text fits is returned whole, whatever its decisions weigh. Both `read_board` descriptions say it. Test: `operator-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 579: a clipped goal keeps every decision recorded on it, whole" (one decision in each separator; canary: the bare excerpt returned). (`app/server/tasks/board-read.server.ts`.)

580. **A knowledge-base document is read in pages** (AWS calculator board, 2026-09-29; extends rulings 283 and 578). `read_knowledge_doc` returned a document's first 48,000 characters and said it was cut, with no way to read on; the controller's org-admin `read_knowledge_base_doc` returned up to 256 KB in one piece. Live, the controller could not take in `calculator.md` (94 KB) and so could not safely apply AWSC-17's 138 corrections to it (a whole-document replace destroys what the writer did not read), and the Workflow Researchers on AWSC-16 and AWSC-17 read past 48,000 characters from disk, which a private knowledge base (ruling 578) closes to every shell. Decided: every `read_knowledge_doc` (agent, operator and controller; `readKbDocForRun`) and the controller's `read_knowledge_base_doc` take an `offset`. The agents' reader returns 48,000 characters from it and, when more remain, says "characters A to B of N in `doc`: what is above is not the whole document; read on with offset B"; its last page says it is the end, and an offset past the end is refused with the document's length. The controller's reader returns `characters`, `offset` and `nextOffset` (null at the end) beside the page, and its description says a whole-document replace needs every page. Tests: `kb-injection.server.test.ts` "ruling 580: a long document is read in pages …" and `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 580: read_knowledge_base_doc returns a long document in pages …"; canaries: `offset` ignored, the whole text returned. (`app/server/files/kb-injection.server.ts`, `app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/agent-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`.)

581. **A knowledge-base correction can delete a passage, and its record takes the lines around it when its text alone would not stand once** (AWS calculator board, AWSC-18, 2026-09-29; amends ruling 498). An undo finds a correction by the text it wrote, so `mergeKbCorrection` refused any text that would not stand exactly once after the write, and `correctKnowledgeDoc` refused an empty `text`. Live on AWSC-18 the Workflow Researcher applied AWSC-17's 138 corrections to `calculator.md`: 39 of them delete a passage, and the tool refused every empty `text` ("needs ... the text to write"), and three more were refused because the corrected text repeated other lines (`live forms` 4 times, a selector twice, ` Evidence:` 56 times). It applied 96 and asked Arda for leave to quote neighbouring characters by hand around the other 42. A second gap sat beside it: a `replaces` not found beside a `text` that stood anywhere in the document was answered "already reads as your `text` ... Nothing needed writing", so a passage one character off could pass for a correction made. Decided: an empty `text` with a `replaces` deletes that passage (the agent tool, the operator tool and the Codex plan's `text`, which says so). The document written is exactly what the filer sent; when the written text is blank or would not stand once, the record names the lines it sits in, taking the lines after and before in turn until the span stands once (where a line runs past 400 characters, characters instead, finishing the word it cut), and records the passage with the same lines around it, so the Controller page's Was and Now read as whole lines and an undo swaps them back. Nothing reaches into a masked proposals section. A match is counted with overlaps, since an undo takes the first one. The same correction made again takes the same lines, so a person's undo still refuses its repeat. A `replaces` that is not in the document is answered from the record: a standing correction whose passage and text hold the ones sent is named ("`kc-...` made this correction ..., and it stands"); otherwise the reply says the passage is not there and, when the text stands elsewhere, how many times, and hands back the closest lines. Tests: `kb-corrections.server.test.ts` "ruling 581: text another line repeats is written ...", "ruling 581: an empty text deletes the passage, a retry finds its record, and an undo puts it back for good", "ruling 581: a passage that is not there is not taken for a made correction ..."; `agent-toolkit.server.test.ts` "rulings 483 and 498: correct_knowledge_doc writes ..." (a deletion); canaries: a split count, a bare record, no retry record, no anchored undo check, the old "already reads" reply, `text` required again. (`app/server/org/kb-corrections.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/kb-correction-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/agent-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/specialist-run.server.ts`, `app/server/seed/assets/viberr-app-expertise.skill.md`.)

582. **A project admin takes a file, or a comment's words, off a task's record** (AWS calculator board, AWSC-19, 2026-09-29). Round 1 left its answer key, `golden-files.md`, in AWSC-3's attachments, where every agent's shell and every `read_board` of that task can read it, and round 3 re-runs the same four samples. On AWSC-19 the Estimate Judge's first report said in words which golden entries price no load-balancer line, on a task every agent can read; the Judge wrote that someone had to remove a file it had posted, "I cannot", and the operator told Arda "A comment is not something I can remove." Nobody could, short of a shell in the container: the timeline was append-only and attachments had writers but no remover. Decided: a new grant, `remove-from-record` (admin only), and two writers beside `attachTaskFile`. `removeTaskAttachment` deletes the file (resolved inside the task's attachments, so a traversing name is refused as absent), takes its name off every entry that claimed it, so no tile opens nothing, and writes an "Attachment removed" note naming the file, its size and the reason; the file goes last, so one that cannot be removed leaves the task file unwritten. `removeTaskComment` finds the comment by its time and puts "Removed by <person> on <day>. Why: <reason>" in place of its text, title and evidence, and of the text of every notification that links to it (`retextEventNotifications`); the entry keeps its time, author and files. Audits `task.attachment.removed` (name, bytes, reason) and `task.comment.removed` (time, author, reason); neither keeps the words. An archived task allows both, since what has to come off the record comes off whatever the task's state; an archived project freezes them like every mutation. The task page offers Remove on the card a file opens in, posted to the task that serves it, and at the end of a comment's row, shown on hover or focus where a pointer can hover, each through the shared confirm with an optional reason (`useRemoveFromRecord`). The operator's skill says a person can do this and that the operator names the file or comment instead of saying nobody can remove it. What the ruling cannot reach: an agent's own run log keeps what that run wrote, and a verdict's stored reason is not a comment. Tests: `record-removal.server.test.ts` (the file and its claims, the refusals, the comment and its notifications, a time holding no comment), `remove-from-record.test.tsx` (both controls, and neither without the grant), and the policy matrix's two drivers; canaries: the claims left, the notifications left, the name resolved without the guard, the card's `removable` dropped, the row's control on typed events. The task route's closure grows by the confirm it shares (`bundle.json`'s raised note). (`app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/projections/notifications.server.ts`, `app/shared/rbac.ts`, `app/routes/project.task.tsx`, `app/features/task-detail/remove-from-record.tsx`, `attachment-lightbox.tsx`, `timeline.tsx`, `app/server/seed/assets/viberr-app-expertise.skill.md`.) **Narrowed by ruling 584** (noted 2026-09-29): a comment's words are no longer a person's to remove; the operator edits or deletes an agent's comment itself, silently, and the task page offers Remove on a file's card only (`remove-from-record` reads "Remove a file from a task").

583. **The operator can run an agent that must not judge, and a verdict with nothing to bind to says so** (AWS calculator board, AWSC-19, 2026-09-29; extends rulings 313 and 316). On AWSC-19 the Estimate Judge ran as a supporting agent writing golden-set corrections on a task Arda closes by force-accept, and the operator's directive said "Record no verdict". The Judge kept to it: it called no `report_outcome` and wrote "No verdict or outcome is recorded, as the directive says". Viberr read one into its report anyway. The prose fallback runs for a verdict-capable run that fell silent, and the report's heading "Not done or not checked" matched its `not (yet)? done` phrase, so the reply was titled "Review verdict" and a quality event read "Validation: none. Estimate Judge requested changes." There was nothing delivered for it to bind to, so the record held no verdict, and the operator had to write on the next packet that the line "is not a verdict". Ruling 316 settled that the guard stops this, not a kinder regex, and gave Viberr's own no-verdict run (the deadlock question) its `withholdVerdict`; an operator directive had no such switch, only a sentence the agent could keep while Viberr still read a verdict into its words. Decided: (a) `run_agent` takes `noVerdict` (the Claude tool, the Codex plan's required field, and a recommendation card, which Apply honours), dispatched as `withholdVerdict`: the run gets no verdict channel and is marked `verdict_withheld`, so the fallback never runs on it; its description says when to pass it (a verdict-capable agent run for its corrections or files on a task a person force-accepts, or a question put before any verdict). (b) A request-changes with nothing delivered to bind to, like an approval with none, is recorded in words only and its note says so: "requested changes, but nothing on this task has been delivered for the verdict to bind to, so it does not count." A prose approval on such a task would still mint ruling R19-8's verification revision, which is what `noVerdict` exists to prevent on the runs the operator tells not to judge. Tests: `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 583: …" (a prompted and a bare run withheld, a plain one not; the Claude tool; a recommended card and its Apply), `operator-run.server.test.ts` (the plan schema's required field, and a Codex plan's `run_agent` marking the run), `no-change-acceptance.server.test.ts` "ruling 583: an objection with nothing delivered says it binds to nothing"; canaries: each of the six threading lines dropped, and the unbound note worded as a bound one. (`app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts`.) Amended 2026-09-29: the controller's `run_agent_on_task` takes `noVerdict` too, for a deployed agent (the operator never judges). Live on AWSC-25 the controller, asked to start the Estimate Judge without a verdict, found its own dispatch had no such switch and asked the task's operator to do it. Test: `controller-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 583: run_agent_on_task withholds the verdict of a run that must not judge"; canary: the switch dropped.

584. **The operator edits or deletes an agent's comment on its task, itself and silently** (owner, 2026-09-29: "operator decides if it's own comments needs deleting or editing. Don't expose this to the end user, fixes the problem silently with mcp and doing it itself, not asking the user"; narrows ruling 582). Ruling 582 gave a project admin a Remove on a comment's row, after the Estimate Judge's report on AWSC-19 named expected rows in words and the operator told Arda "A comment is not something I can remove". The owner moved the comment to the operator. Decided: the operator's `edit_comment` (the Claude tool, and the Codex plan's `edit_comment` with a required `commentAt`), on its `append-typed-events` grant, edits or deletes a comment the operator or an agent wrote on its task (`operatorEditComment`): an edit replaces the words and keeps the author, time, title and files; a delete takes the entry off the timeline. A person's comment is refused. The notifications that link to it follow (`followEditedComment`): a mention quotes the new words, and every row about a deleted comment goes. Nothing on the task or in an inbox says so; audit `task.comment.edited` or `task.comment.deleted` keeps the time, the author and the operator's reason, never the words. The operator's skill says to use it without asking anyone and without saying so. The person's comment Remove, its route intent, its writer and its stylesheet rule are gone; files keep ruling 582's Remove. Tests: `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 584: …" (an edit that says nothing and requotes the mention, a delete that takes the notifications with it, a person's comment and a missing time refused, the Claude tool and its grant), `operator-run.server.test.ts` (the plan's `commentAt` and tool); canaries: a note written, the notifications left, the author check dropped, the plan's tool dropped. (`app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts`, `app/server/projections/notifications.server.ts`, `app/features/task-detail/timeline.tsx`, `app/server/seed/assets/viberr-app-expertise.skill.md`.)

585. **A Codex specialist reads and corrects its knowledge bases through Viberr's gateway** (owner, 2026-09-29: "change agents back to gpt 6 luna max"; completes ruling 578 and extends rulings 422, 461 and 498). Moving the AWS calculator board's five agents back to Codex GPT-6 Luna, the controller moved four and kept the Estimate Judge on Claude: the golden set it scores against is a private knowledge base (ruling 578), a private folder is closed to every shell, and a Codex specialist mounts no in-process Viberr tools (ruling 422), so on Luna the Judge would have been told the grant could not reach it. It offered the owner a Judge on Claude, an open answer key every agent's shell could read, or a Judge that could not score. The same gap reached further: a Codex specialist has no `correct_knowledge_doc` either, so it reports a correction in its final reply for the operator to write (ruling 483). For a private knowledge base that puts the passage on the task, where every agent reads, and for the four agents moving back it would have replaced the direct corrections they made on Claude (one AWSC-18 run made 103) with an operator turn each. Decided: Viberr's MCP gateway (ruling 461) answers one more server itself, `viberr_knowledge` (reserved, both spellings), with the two knowledge tools a Claude specialist's toolkit holds. A Codex specialist that holds any knowledge base mounts it, fresh and resumed (`resolveKnowledgeMcp`), at the gateway's own URL. The mount carries the run's knowledge bases, its store and its agent to the gateway; `startRun`'s binding keeps them there and hands the run only the URL and its run token. `read_knowledge_doc` is answered by the same reader as Claude's (`readKbDocForRun`: the same pages, ruling 580, and the same refusal for a knowledge base the run was not given), and `correct_knowledge_doc` by the same writer (`correctKnowledgeDoc`, ruling 498), as the run's agent on the run's task. Their arguments are parsed where the gateway receives the call, each call is logged like every gateway call without its arguments or result, a run whose calls have closed calls nothing, and the token dies with the run. The run's index sends it to `read_knowledge_doc` for a private folder, and its Collaboration section names the tool instead of the report section. A Claude run mounts nothing new, an open knowledge base still reaches a Codex run at its folder path too (ruling 422), and with the gateway not running a Codex run keeps the old channels: its folders, the report section, and a private knowledge base as an unresolved grant with its reason. The controller's `save_knowledge_base` `private` description says a Codex specialist reads through the gateway. Tests: `gateway-runs.server.test.ts` "ruling 585: the gateway answers a Codex run's knowledge server itself" (no mount on Claude or without a knowledge base, the run handed only the URL and token, both tools listed, the private document read, another knowledge base refused, a correction written into the private document as the Codex agent, 401 after the run ends); `specialist-run.server.test.ts` "ruling 585: a Codex run that holds a knowledge base mounts the gateway's knowledge server, fresh and resumed" (the mount, the private index, the tool's correction note, the run record, the resumed run's mount and prompt) and the ruling 578 persona test's Codex-with-the-tool case. Canaries: the gateway's own branch skipped, the no-knowledge-base check dropped, the mount's list left on the run's config, the correction written as another backend's agent, either path's mount dropped, the persona or the correction note ignoring the mount. (`app/server/mcp-proxy/knowledge-tool.server.ts`, `app/server/mcp-proxy/gateway.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/specialist-mcp.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/specialist-run.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/agent-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/shared/mcp-reserved.ts`.)

586. **The entry that records a question carries the card, which leaves the task when it is answered** (AWSC-22, 2026-09-29). An agent's question and the operator's decision packet each write an entry when they open, and it named only the card's title: "**Question for a human:** AWSC-22 Intake batch: accept the proposed defaults, or change numbered items?". The card's body, twenty-five numbered questions with their proposed defaults, lived on the packet, and a packet leaves the task when it is answered; the decision entry records the chosen option and the person's words. So once Arda answered, what the customer had been asked was on no record, and the board's goal is that its agents "ask correct questions in every step". Reviewing AWSC-22 at 100/100, the Estimate Judge could not check that each intake question asked one thing: "This is unverified against the card text, which is not on the task". Decided: the three writers of a question's entry (`ask_human`, the Codex outcome envelope's question and `operatorOpenPacket`) write the card on it with `askedEntryText`: the heading, then the body as the asker wrote it, the observations, and the options with the recommended one marked (a lone "Answer the question" is not listed). The heading takes the title as a sentence and adds no second mark after a question mark ("Which region do we price? Awaiting a human decision."). Viberr's own recovery packets (a failed run, a stall, a conflict, the review deadlock) restate facts already on the timeline and keep their one-line entries, and the decision entry is unchanged. A long typed entry now folds behind its own Show more, as a comment does (ruling 510). Tests: `agent-toolkit.server.test.ts` "ruling 478(e) …" (the Claude entry), `agent-completion.server.test.ts` "ruling 586: the question's entry carries the card …", `operator-actions.server.test.ts` "ruling 586: the operator's decision entry carries its card …" and `task-detail-components.test.tsx` "ruling 586: a long typed entry folds …". Canaries: either agent writer or the operator's back to its title alone, the doubled mark restored, the typed entry never folding. (`app/server/tasks/agent-outcome.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/agent-toolkit.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts`, `app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts`, `app/features/task-detail/timeline.tsx`.)

## Notes appended after the rulings

*(Moved here 2026-09-23 by the documentation sweep, verbatim. They used to sit between ruling 201
and the route map, where the rulings had been appended out of order.)*

F36-6 (pass 36, amends F19-1): Viberr's own delivery next-step card is written only for
a verdict-clean revision (`healthy`, or a project with no verdict-capable specialist); a
`failing` or pending verdict withholds it with a `github.delivery.next_step {withheld}`
audit row, and a request-changes verdict drops any pending transition card the same way
it already dropped the accept offer. "Review stage" in that writer is the stage with an
edge into the terminal one, so a task AT its verdict stage was "strictly before" it.

*(Documentation drift closed by pass 35, recorded 2026-09-07. The pass-35 discovery read
found five places where a page or a sentence said something the code did not. Each is
corrected on the page named; the note stays here so a reader who meets the old wording, in
a ledger or in an older branch, can see when it stopped being true. Drift ids are the
discovery index's, `planning/discovery-2026-09-06-pass35-k9s-clone/reference/INDEX.md`.)*

- **D14** — `docs/README.md` said the controller had "38 tools" while 39 were registered
  and `controller-and-goals.md` said 39. Ruling 153 adds `schedule_task_action` and
  `cancel_task_schedule`, so the number is now **41** and both pages say it; the count is
  `grep -c "^  add(" app/server/controller/controller-toolkit.server.ts`. *(That command
  counts 51 at `7d9fbf72`, 2026-09-23.)*
- **D22** — `docs/architecture/data-model.md`'s `instance_settings` row named quota keys the
  writer never used. It now names the three live keys as `backend-quota.server.ts` writes
  them (`backendRateLimit.<backend>`, `backendQuotaExhausted.<backend>` with `resetsAt` and
  its `resetsAtPrecision`, and `backendCredentialRefused.<backend>`), each carrying the
  account it billed since ruling 130(d).
- **D40** — no page said `users.github_handle` had exactly ONE writer, GitHub OAuth
  sign-in, so ruling 68's human-approval verdict was unreachable on a deployment that signs
  in locally. Ruling 154 gives the column its second writer and the org admin's door;
  `github-delivery.md` §10 records the correction, and §5 now lists every writer. *(2026-09-23: §10 was removed by the documentation sweep; the correction is stated in §5.)*
- **D88** — the `unlinked_handle` refusal told people to "link it on their profile", while
  the profile card on an OAuth-less deployment offered nothing to connect. Ruling 154's
  sentence names both doors: Org settings, Users & access, and the profile where GitHub
  sign-in is configured.
- **D97** — the stage-eligibility refusal printed the raw stage id (`impl`) where a person
  reads a name. `stageRefusalSentence` (`app/server/tasks/specialist-run.server.ts`) resolves
  both the task's stage and the profile's declared stages through the board, which is also
  what makes F35-5's "Mention not started" timeline note readable.

## Owner decisions recorded outside this file (2026-08-20 → 2026-09-01)

*(Added 2026-09-01 by the documentation validation pass. Each item below is an owner decision
that code comments or pass ledgers cite and that this file never received. They are listed
here so a reader can find them; promoting each to a numbered ruling is the owner's call —
ruling 44 says every one should be. Where recorded today is named per item.)*

   the single source of "withheld when absent"; `use-web-search-fetch` is not in it, so an
   absent grant leaves egress on. `app/shared/capabilities.ts`; pass-23 FINDINGS.

   Codex operator's writable root is an empty `.operator-scratch` beside `task.md`; its web
   search follows `use-web-search-fetch`. `operator-run.server.ts`; pass-24 QUESTIONS.
   *(Corrected 2026-09-23: since ruling 185 every Codex thread is `danger-full-access`, so
   `.operator-scratch` is the operator's working directory and nothing refuses a write outside
   it; ruling 207(b) removed the prompt's claim that it did.)*

## Route map

```
/login  /logout  /api/auth/*            (better-auth, incl. OAuth callbacks)
/                                       → home (project list)
/projects                               → redirect to / (bare /projects is not a 404 — N5)
/projects/:slug                         → redirect to board
/projects/:slug/board  /review  /controller  /agents  /policy  /github  /activity  /settings
/projects/:slug/tasks/:key
/projects/:slug/tasks/:key/attachments/:file   (R19-19 — member-only, raw bytes)
/org/settings                           (org admin, tabbed — incl. the Controller tab)
/org/settings/audit-export              (org admin — CSV/JSON audit download, pass 26)
/controller                             (ruling 99 — every signed-in user)
/insights                               (org admin — run analytics, pass 29)
/profile   /notifications   /notifications/read   /prefs/theme
/resources/events  (SSE)   /resources/health   /resources/run-log
/resources/search   /resources/session-export   /resources/model-catalog
/resources/controller                   (ruling 121 — the dock's GET view + POST send)
/resources/controller-unseen            (ruling 448 — the viewer's unseen controller replies)
/resources/backend-login                (ruling 127 — the signed-in viewer's own sign-in session)
```

*(Regenerated 2026-09-23 from `app/routes.ts`, which is the source of truth. `/org/settings`,
`/controller`, `/insights`, `/profile` and `/notifications` render inside the pathless
`palette-shell` layout (ruling 145); `/projects/:slug/*` inside the `project.tsx` workspace
shell. `/resources/backend-login` answers `GET ?backend=claude|codex` behind `requireUser` with
the CALLER's own live sign-in session and the public half of their `userBackendHealth`, and
reads nobody else's. The per-route guard and form-intent inventory is in
[`../ui/surfaces.md`](../ui/surfaces.md).)*
